method: They use nonlinear photonic spacetime crystals with a complete energy-momentum gap to suppress radiation, and Kerr self-trapping to localize events. Symmetry constraints are imposed and relaxed to generate multipole and vortex states, and they analyze their spectra and robustness.
result: They predict structured events with transverse scales of 30-60 μm and temporal durations of 85-170 fs, and distinguish phase-winding vortices from real-valued multipoles via Bogoliubov-de Gennes spectra.
conclusion: Events can be treated as controllable localized wave objects, offering a route to wave control in nonlinear time-varying media.

title: Solitons In Optical Couplers: Introduction And Perspectives
authors: Boris A. Malomed
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00696v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This minireview provides a brief summary and a discussion of directions for further development of theoretical and, chiefly, experimental studies of bright solitons in optical couplers, i.e., dual-core waveguides which combine the linear inter-core coupling (tunneling of light between the parallel cores with the intra-core group-velocity dispersion and self-focusing Kerr (cubic) nonlinearity. Following a short introduction to the field, the article focuses on a brief review of relatively recent experimental results for the switching of solitons in dual-core nonlinear optical fibers and the spontaneous emergence of stable asymmetric two-core solitons in the couplers with the symmetric dual-core structure.
tldr: A minireview on bright solitons in optical couplers, focusing on experimental results and future directions.
motivation: To summarize recent progress and outline perspectives for soliton switching and spontaneous symmetry breaking in dual-core nonlinear fibers.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental studies on solitons in optical couplers, with emphasis on recent experiments.
result: Highlights experimental demonstrations of soliton switching and stable asymmetric solitons in symmetric couplers.
conclusion: The field offers promising directions for further experimental and theoretical work, particularly in nonlinear photonics.

title: Efficient Mode Conversion At 1064 Nm Via Bilayer Inverse Taper On Thin-Film Lithium Niobate
authors: Ruidong Xue, Jobayer Hossain, Joshua Arnold, Jiuyi Zhang, Xiaofeng Zhu, Marco Moller de Freitas, Christopher J. Cullen, Shouyuan Shi, Peng Yao, Timothy Creazzo, Dennis Prather
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient fiber-to-chip coupling remains challenging for thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) devices operating at 1064 nm. Here, we fabricate and characterize an on-chip optical mode converter based on a bilayer inverse taper. The proposed structure demonstrated a coupling loss of 1.9 dB per facet for the TE mode, with a 1 dB bandwidth spanning 1055--1085 nm. The polarization-dependent alignment tolerance was measured along the lateral and vertical directions. Theoretical and simulation analyses indicate that, when using a lensed fiber with a mode field diameter of 2.5 [MATH]m, the coupling loss can be reduced to as low as 0.48 dB per facet. These results demonstrate the feasibility of providing a high-efficiency solution for on-chip optical coupling at 1064 nm.
tldr: This paper demonstrates an efficient fiber-to-chip mode converter on thin-film lithium niobate at 1064 nm using a bilayer inverse taper, achieving low coupling loss.
motivation: Efficient fiber-to-chip coupling is challenging for TFLN devices at 1064 nm, which is important for quantum and classical photonic applications.
method: The authors fabricate and characterize a bilayer inverse taper structure on TFLN, measuring coupling loss and alignment tolerances, and perform simulations to predict lower losses with a lensed fiber.
result: The device achieves 1.9 dB per facet coupling loss with 1 dB bandwidth of 1055-1085 nm, and simulations suggest 0.48 dB per facet with a 2.5 μm MFD lensed fiber.
conclusion: The bilayer inverse taper provides a high-efficiency solution for on-chip optical coupling at 1064 nm, potentially benefiting quantum photonic integration.

title: Phase-continuous Comparison Of Three All-optical Time Scales Over 20 Days
authors: Dahyeon Lee, Kyungtae Kim, Zoey Z. Hu, Ben Lewis, William Warfield, Kai Zhou, Alejandra L. Collopy, Jeffrey A. Sherman, Abijith S. Kowligy, Parth B. Patel, Jonathan D. Roslund, Arman Cing\"oz, Martin M. Boyd, Jun Ye
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical frequency standards have progressed rapidly over the past two decades, leading to the anticipated redefinition of the SI second by an optical frequency. However, time scales have not yet significantly improved despite this development because they are still fully reliant on rf flywheel oscillators, mostly hydrogen masers, which impose a performance limit related to incompletely sampled noise known as the Dick effect. To best benefit from the exceptional stability and accuracy of optical frequency standards, time scales must employ optical flywheels with orders-of-magnitude better short-term (<[MATH] s) stability than masers. Here, we introduce three optical flywheel oscillators (two cryogenic silicon cavities and one iodine optical clock) with superior short-term stability than hydrogen masers and long-term stability on par with masers. Steering each optical flywheel with a high-uptime Sr optical frequency standard generates three parallel all-optical time scales with continuous operation over >20 days. When compared with each other, these all-optical time scales achieve <[MATH] relative instability after just a few days of averaging. During typical steering gaps of ~6 hours, the accumulated time difference is ~20 ps, leading to the total time difference of <100 ps over the full measurement period. With the proliferation of long-distance optical fiber links and commercialization of optical flywheels and frequency standards, we anticipate all-optical time scales to be the future of timekeeping.
tldr: This paper demonstrates continuous operation of three all-optical time scales over 20 days, achieving sub-100 ps time differences, but it is primarily an experimental metrology result with no direct connection to quantum information theory or quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: Optical frequency standards have advanced, but time scales still rely on rf flywheels (hydrogen masers) that limit performance due to the Dick effect. The authors aim to replace these with optical flywheels to improve timekeeping stability.
method: They use two cryogenic silicon cavities and one iodine optical clock as optical flywheels, each steered by a Sr optical frequency standard, and compare the resulting time scales over a 20-day continuous run.
result: The all-optical time scales achieve relative instability below 10^-16 after a few days, with accumulated time differences of ~20 ps during 6-hour steering gaps and <100 ps over the full period.
conclusion: All-optical time scales are viable and superior to maser-based systems, suggesting they will become the future of timekeeping as optical links and flywheels become more widespread.

title: Operators On Anti-dual Pairs: Means Of Positive Operators
authors: \'abel G\"ode Zsigmond Tarcsay
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00031v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a theory of Kubo-Ando type means for positive operators on anti-dual pairs. This framework extends the classical theory of operator means beyond bounded Hilbert space operators and provides a common setting for several concrete classes of positive objects, including nonnegative sesquilinear forms and states on [MATH]-algebras. We also introduce a Busch-Gudder type strength function for positive operators on anti-dual pairs and investigate its interaction with operator means. Applications are given to Hilbert space operators, nonnegative forms, and representable positive functionals.
tldr: This paper develops a theory of Kubo-Ando type means for positive operators on anti-dual pairs, extending operator means beyond bounded Hilbert space operators.
motivation: The authors aim to generalize the classical theory of operator means to a broader framework that includes nonnegative sesquilinear forms and states on C*-algebras, providing a unified setting for various positive objects.
method: They introduce a theory of means for positive operators on anti-dual pairs, and also define a Busch-Gudder type strength function, investigating its interaction with these means.
result: The framework provides a common setting for several concrete classes of positive objects, with applications to Hilbert space operators, nonnegative forms, and representable positive functionals.
conclusion: The work extends operator mean theory to a more general context, but it is primarily a mathematical contribution without direct connection to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Continuity Of Measure-theoretic Entropy For Stochastic Differential Equations
authors: Lixin Zhang Zhenxin Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For stochastic differential equations, we establish a relationship between the measure-theoretic entropy of the stochastic flow and the rate of volume growth of stable submanifolds under iteration. By combining the result of Kifer and Yomdin (1988), we show that under a suitable integrability condition, for systems with [MATH] coefficients, the measure-theoretic entropy is upper semicontinuous with respect to the coefficients of SDEs.
tldr: This paper studies the continuity of measure-theoretic entropy for stochastic differential equations, linking it to volume growth of stable manifolds.
motivation: The authors aim to establish semicontinuity properties of entropy for SDEs, extending deterministic results to stochastic settings.
method: They combine results from Kifer and Yomdin (1988) and analyze the relationship between entropy and volume growth of stable submanifolds under iteration.
result: Under suitable integrability conditions, they show that measure-theoretic entropy is upper semicontinuous with respect to the coefficients of SDEs.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical foundation for understanding entropy in stochastic dynamical systems, but it is not directly connected to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Gnn-rsma: An Interference Management Framework For A Large-Scale Haps Network
authors: Afsoon Alidadi Shamsabadi, Animesh Yadav, Halim Yanikomeroglu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrating non-terrestrial networks (NTN) with terrestrial infrastructure is a key enabler of next-generation wireless systems, providing ubiquitous connectivity while meeting stringent rate and latency requirements. In particular, high altitude platform stations (HAPS) can complement terrestrial networks and jointly form vertical heterogeneous networks (vHetNets), extending coverage while delivering high-capacity, reliable, and low-latency connectivity for user equipments (UEs) including ground users and uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs). However, the high altitude deployment of HAPS establishes strong line-of-sight (LoS) links to UEs, creating highly correlated channels among UEs. Moreover, the wide coverage footprint of HAPS enables it to serve a large number of UEs, forcing limited radio resources to be shared among many UEs and resulting in significant intra-resource block (RB) interference. To address this challenge, we propose an interference management scheme based on UE clustering and rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA). Specifically, the network is modeled as a heterogeneous graph, and a graph neural network (GNN) is developed to efficiently allocate the common and private RSMA powers, maximizing the minimum spectral efficiency (SE) in a fast and scalable manner. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed GNN-RSMA interference management algorithm outperforms conventional multiple access schemes while achieving fairness and worst-user performance comparable to successive convex approximation (SCA)-based optimization at only a fraction of its computational cost.
tldr: This paper proposes a GNN-based interference management framework using rate-splitting multiple access for large-scale HAPS networks.
motivation: High altitude platform stations (HAPS) create strong line-of-sight links and serve many users, leading to significant interference that needs efficient management.
method: The network is modeled as a heterogeneous graph, and a graph neural network (GNN) is developed to allocate common and private RSMA powers to maximize minimum spectral efficiency.
result: Simulations show the GNN-RSMA algorithm outperforms conventional multiple access schemes and achieves fairness and worst-user performance comparable to SCA-based optimization at lower computational cost.
conclusion: The proposed method offers a fast and scalable interference management solution for HAPS networks.

title: Channel-Agnostic Semantic Compression For Bandwidth-Limited Visual Communication
authors: Xuanhao Luo, Ruichen Gao, Zhizhen Li, Mingzhe Chen, Yuchen Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Bandwidth-limited visual communication systems require efficient transmission of high-dimensional data under dynamic wireless conditions. Existing approaches either rely on joint source-channel coding, which tightly couples representation learning with channel models and lacks flexibility across varying environments, or adopt generative reconstruction techniques that may introduce semantically inconsistent outputs. In this paper, we propose RQ-NAC, a channel-agnostic semantic compression framework for visual communication. The proposed method leverages residual quantization to produce scalable discrete semantic representations, enabling fine-grained and predictable control over the rate-distortion tradeoff. To further enhance compression efficiency, we integrate an n-gram-driven arithmetic coding module that exploits contextual dependencies among latent indices for lossless entropy coding. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RQ-NAC achieves over 600[MATH] compression relative to uncompressed visual data while preserving high perceptual quality. The results show that our approach enables efficient, flexible, and reliable semantic transmission under bandwidth-constrained conditions.
tldr: This paper proposes a channel-agnostic semantic compression framework for visual communication using residual quantization and n-gram arithmetic coding.
motivation: Bandwidth-limited visual communication requires efficient transmission, but existing joint source-channel coding lacks flexibility and generative methods may produce inconsistent outputs.
method: RQ-NAC uses residual quantization to create scalable discrete semantic representations and integrates n-gram-driven arithmetic coding for lossless entropy coding.
result: Achieves over 600x compression relative to uncompressed data while preserving high perceptual quality.
conclusion: The approach enables efficient, flexible, and reliable semantic transmission under bandwidth-constrained conditions.

title: Structure-Preserving Dynamical Low-Rank Approximations For Stochastic Vlasov--Poisson Equations
authors: Carmela Scalone Jianbo Cui
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00397v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose structure-preserving dynamical low-rank methods for stochastic Vlasov--Poisson equations with transport noise. We first derive the continuous low-rank evolution equations and show that, by including fixed velocity modes associated with the conserved quantities, the low-rank dynamics inherits the mass, momentum, and energy balance laws of the original stochastic model. We then develop two augmented basis-update Galerkin (BUG) integrators based on two stochastic discretizations: an Euler--Maruyama scheme applied to the equivalent It\^o formulation and a Heun scheme applied directly to the Stratonovich formulation. These two choices allow us to study how the stochastic time discretization interacts with the conservative low-rank framework. In both cases, basis augmentation and conservative rank truncation retain the relevant moment spaces and provide robustness under rank reduction. Numerical experiments demonstrate the conservation properties of the proposed methods and compare the augmentation requirements, stochastic correction terms, and momentum and energy behavior induced by the two stochastic formulations.
tldr: This paper proposes structure-preserving dynamical low-rank methods for stochastic Vlasov-Poisson equations, focusing on numerical methods for plasma physics.
motivation: The authors aim to develop efficient numerical methods for stochastic kinetic equations that preserve physical conservation laws.
method: They derive continuous low-rank evolution equations and develop two augmented basis-update Galerkin integrators based on Euler-Maruyama and Heun schemes.
result: Numerical experiments demonstrate conservation properties and compare the two stochastic discretizations.
conclusion: The proposed methods are robust and preserve mass, momentum, and energy, but the topic is far from the user's research interests.

title: Infinite-Piecewise Expanding Maps: Chaos, Ergodicity And Invariant-Set Complexity
authors: Matheus G. C. Cunha, Douglas D. Novaes, Gabriel Ponce
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00398v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study a class of one-dimensional piecewise maps defined by infinitely many smooth expanding branches. This class arises naturally in the context of non-smooth dynamical systems and includes the first-return maps locally defined near sliding Shilnikov connections. By means of the theory of conformal iterated function systems (CIFS), we investigate several dynamical properties of these maps as well as the topological complexity of their invariant sets. In particular, we show that the dynamics restricted to the invariant set is topologically conjugate to the shift on [MATH]. We also establish the existence of a unique conformal measure that is invariant and ergodic under the map.
tldr: This paper studies infinite-piecewise expanding maps and their ergodic properties using conformal iterated function systems, focusing on topological conjugacy to a shift and existence of invariant measures.
motivation: The class of maps arises from non-smooth dynamical systems, particularly near sliding Shilnikov connections, and the authors aim to understand their dynamical properties and invariant set complexity.
method: The authors employ the theory of conformal iterated function systems (CIFS) to analyze the maps, proving topological conjugacy to a shift and establishing existence of a unique conformal measure.
result: They show the dynamics on the invariant set is topologically conjugate to a shift, and there exists a unique conformal measure that is invariant and ergodic.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of piecewise expanding maps and conformal measures, but it is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Frequency Coding Over Noisy Sampling
authors: Bo-Yu Su, Hsin-Po Wang, Venkatesan Guruswami
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: DNA molecules are so small that it might be practical to use their frequency vectors to encode messages. More precisely, a sender can inject [MATH] copies of the string [MATH] CATCATCAT into a pool and the receiver can recover [MATH] by sequencing the pool. There are, however, two sources of uncertainty: (a) [MATH] is usually too big to be counted exactly, but is estimated by sampling. (b) The DNA sequencer could be noisy; it may have difficulty distinguishing CATCATCAT from CATGATCAT. Recently, Tamir, Weinberger, and Guill\'en i F\`abregas clarified the amount of information the frequency vector can carry under (a). They showed that each string can carry about [MATH] bits, where [MATH] is the average number of times each string is read. They also showed that [MATH] bits can be achieved by a low-complexity uncoded scheme under the condition that there are at least [MATH] distinct strings. In this paper, we show that a low-complexity coded scheme can achieve the same [MATH] bits unconditionally. We then generalize the scheme to handle sequencing noise, (b), and show that the noise penalizes the total number of bits by [MATH], together with a linear term due to the use of Fourier transforms in our proof. The former penalty [MATH] is asymptotically the same as that obtained by Gerzon, Shomorony, and Weinberger; our scheme trades a small amount of rate for practical complexity.
tldr: This paper studies coding schemes for DNA storage using frequency vectors, focusing on information-theoretic limits under sampling and sequencing noise.
motivation: The authors aim to improve the achievable rate of DNA-based data storage by designing low-complexity coded schemes that handle both sampling noise and sequencing errors.
method: They propose a coded scheme based on Fourier transforms that achieves the same asymptotic rate as an uncoded scheme but without requiring a large number of distinct strings, and extend it to handle sequencing noise.
result: The coded scheme achieves the optimal rate unconditionally, and the noise penalty is characterized, matching prior bounds with a trade-off of rate for practical complexity.
conclusion: The work provides a practical coding approach for DNA storage, but it is not aligned with the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: An Information Theoretic Treatment Of Yager's Probability Distribution Negation
authors: Ugo Vaccaro Roberto Bruno
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00594v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the seminal paper (Yager 2015), Yager defined the negation of a probability distribution [MATH], as the distribution [MATH], where [MATH] for [MATH] In this paper, we present a comprehensive information-theoretic analysis of Yager's negation and its generalizations. Using tools from information theory and majorization theory, we unify, extend, and strengthen a number of previously known properties of Yager's negation within a common framework. Overall, our results offer strong theoretical justification for Yager's negation as the most natural and principled definition of probability distribution negation under various information theoretic criteria.
tldr: This paper provides an information-theoretic analysis of Yager's negation of probability distributions, unifying and extending known properties using majorization theory.
motivation: The authors aim to provide a principled justification for Yager's negation as the most natural definition of probability distribution negation, based on information-theoretic criteria.
method: The paper employs tools from information theory and majorization theory to analyze Yager's negation and its generalizations, unifying and strengthening previous results.
result: The analysis yields a comprehensive framework that confirms and extends properties of Yager's negation, offering theoretical justification for its use.
conclusion: The results strongly support Yager's negation as a natural and principled definition under various information-theoretic criteria.

title: Spectral Algorithms For 3-Wave Kinetic And $c_{12}$ Quantum Boltzmann Equations With General Resonance Manifolds In $\mathbb{R}^d$
authors: Minh-Binh Tran Thanh Trung Le
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Following recent developments in numerical schemes for 3-wave kinetic equations [2, 7, 42, 44, 43], we develop spectral algorithms for multidimensional 3-wave kinetic equations and [MATH] quantum Boltzmann equations with general polynomial dispersion relations. The principal numerical difficulty arises from the resonance constraint, supported on a nonlinear manifold in wave-vector space. We approximate the Dirac distribution by a truncated Fourier representation and derive two spectral discretizations of the collision operator. The first is a direct spectral method with complexity [MATH], while the second exploits multidimensional FFTs to reduce the complexity to [MATH]. Numerical tests show excellent agreement between the two methods, with the fast algorithm providing substantial computational savings. To suppress unresolved high-frequency modes, we combine the classical [MATH]-rule with exponential spectral filtering. Simulations in two and three dimensions capture the gain--loss dynamics of the [MATH] quantum Boltzmann equation for both rapidly and algebraically decaying initial data. For the 3-wave kinetic equation, the computations exhibit strong oscillations and rapid spectral broadening, providing numerical evidence of an apparent energy cascade toward high frequencies. The results also show that the dispersion relation and spatial dimension strongly influence the transient resonant dynamics.
tldr: This paper develops spectral algorithms for solving multidimensional 3-wave kinetic and quantum Boltzmann equations with general resonance manifolds.
motivation: The numerical challenge of handling resonance constraints in kinetic equations motivates the development of efficient spectral methods.
method: The authors approximate the Dirac distribution via truncated Fourier representation and derive two spectral discretizations, one direct and one using multidimensional FFTs, with exponential spectral filtering.
result: Numerical tests show excellent agreement between the two methods, with the fast algorithm providing substantial computational savings, and simulations capture gain-loss dynamics and energy cascades.
conclusion: The proposed spectral algorithms are efficient and accurate for simulating kinetic equations, with results influenced by dispersion relation and spatial dimension.

title: Variational Inference Using A Differentiable Multigrid Linear Solver
authors: Andr\'es Ram\'irez, Philipp Haim, David F\"oger, Torsten A. En{\ss}lin, Philipp Frank, Philipp Gschwandtner, Dominik J\"ustel, Philipp Mertsch, Vo Hong Minh Phan, Laurin S\"oding, Hanieh Zandinejad, Ralf Kissmann
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00760v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gradient-based Bayesian inference methods require efficient access to Jacobian and adjoint-Jacobian operators of high-dimensional forward models. While multigrid solvers provide near-optimal complexity for elliptic partial differential equations, they are rarely available in forms compatible with automatic differentiation (AD). We develop a differentiable multigrid solver for steady-state diffusion-absorption problems and derive its adjoint operations analytically through the full multigrid hierarchy. The resulting solver, DMGS, is implemented in C++ and interfaced with JAX to provide efficient Jacobian-vector and vector-Jacobian products for variational inference in the NIFTy framework. We validate the approach on a 3D inverse problem involving diffuse radiative transfer in tissue, reconstructing an effective radiative source from Monte Carlo-simulated data. The reconstruction reproduces the data at a reduced chi-squared of 1.1 and generalizes to 32 independent validation datasets. Benchmarks against a JAX-native multigrid implementation show comparable runtimes and consistently lower peak memory for the hand-derived adjoint, with modest reverse-mode overhead. These results establish differentiable multigrid solvers as practical building blocks for variational inference in PDE-constrained problems.
tldr: This paper presents a differentiable multigrid solver for efficient variational inference in PDE-constrained inverse problems, applied to diffuse radiative transfer.
motivation: Gradient-based Bayesian inference requires efficient Jacobian operations for high-dimensional forward models, but multigrid solvers are rarely AD-compatible.
method: The authors develop a differentiable multigrid solver (DMGS) in C++ with JAX interface, deriving adjoint operations analytically through the multigrid hierarchy.
result: The solver achieves reduced chi-squared of 1.1 on a 3D inverse problem and shows comparable runtimes with lower memory than a JAX-native implementation.
conclusion: Differentiable multigrid solvers are practical for variational inference in PDE-constrained problems, but the topic is outside the specified research directions.

title: New Results Towards The Characterization Of Service Rate Region Of Reed-Muller Codes
authors: Chenyang Yu, Luopeng Sun, Yiwei Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Service Rate Region (SRR) serves as a critical metric for evaluating the concurrent service capacity of distributed storage systems. While several works have characterized the SRR for MDS codes and first order Reed-Muller codes, for high-order Reed-Muller codes the problem becomes way more complicated and only partial results were given by Ly, Soljanin, and Lalitha [IEEE ISIT 2025]. In this paper, we refine the SRR analysis by explicitly characterizing the intersection patterns of recovery sets for high-order Reed-Muller codes, deriving the exact region for the case m=r+1 and providing new types of strictly tighter constraints to bridge the gap between existing approximations and the exact SRR polytope.
tldr: This paper characterizes the service rate region of high-order Reed-Muller codes for distributed storage systems, refining intersection patterns and deriving tighter constraints.
motivation: The service rate region is critical for evaluating concurrent service capacity in distributed storage, but high-order Reed-Muller codes lack exact characterization.
method: The authors explicitly characterize intersection patterns of recovery sets for high-order Reed-Muller codes and derive the exact region for m=r+1, along with new tighter constraints.
result: They obtain the exact SRR for m=r+1 and provide new types of strictly tighter constraints that bridge the gap between approximations and the exact polytope.
conclusion: This work advances the theoretical understanding of service rate regions for Reed-Muller codes, though it is not directly related to the user's research interests.

title: Partially-Observable Transmission Control For UAV-Enabled Federated Learning In IoT Networks
authors: Masoud Ghazikor, Zhou Ni, Morteza Hashemi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-enabled federated learning (FL) can provide flexible, on-demand edge intelligence for large-scale IoT deployments, but operating in shared unlicensed bands makes uplink update delivery interference-coupled and unreliable. In this paper, we develop a packet-level transmission framework that captures buffer overflow, delay violations, and transmission errors, and uses the resulting packet delivery ratio (PDR) to represent partial-update reception through a packetized, Bernoulli-masked FL aggregation process. We then formulate a fairness-consensus bilevel (FCB) optimization that jointly controls (i) transmission thresholds to maximize the average PDR while reaching consensus under partial observability and (ii) transmission powers to improve the worst PDR and enforce fairness across IoT learners. To solve this problem, we propose an alternating FCB optimizer composed of a consensus-based threshold controller (CTC), which drives the IoT learners toward a PDR-efficient consensus on transmission thresholds, and a fairness-based power controller (FPC), which updates transmission powers to improve the worst PDR and ensure fairness under the resulting consensus thresholds. Numerical results on CNN-based FL tasks show that the FCB optimizer improves FL aggregation and training performance by enhancing packet-level update delivery, consistently outperforming baseline transmission policies.
tldr: This paper proposes a transmission control framework for UAV-enabled federated learning in IoT networks, focusing on packet-level delivery and fairness.
motivation: UAV-enabled federated learning in IoT networks suffers from unreliable uplink transmissions due to interference, leading to partial updates and degraded performance.
method: The authors model packet delivery with a Bernoulli-masked aggregation process and formulate a fairness-consensus bilevel optimization to jointly control transmission thresholds and powers, solved via an alternating optimizer.
result: Numerical results on CNN-based FL tasks show improved aggregation and training performance compared to baseline policies.
conclusion: The proposed framework enhances FL performance by improving packet-level update delivery in UAV-enabled IoT networks.

title: Goal-Oriented Logic-based Semantic Communication For Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning With Applications Onto Autonomous Driving
authors: Ahmet Faruk Saz, Duo Xu, Faramarz Fekri
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00878v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider First-Order Logic (FOL)-based semantic communication for neuro-symbolic decision-making in collaborative environments such as autonomous driving networks. Each connected autonomous vehicle (CAV) converts its partial sensor observations into a natural-language scene description and corresponding grounded FOL evidence. Under an uplink budget, a semantic encoder at each car selects the observations most informative for evaluating traffic rules and transmit to a Road Side Unit (RSU). The RSU fuses all received evidence, evaluates collaborative rules, performs logical deduction for vehicle-specific safety and right-of-way information for constrained downlink transmission. Each CAV combines the received deductions with its local description, enabling a local LLM agent to select a high-level driving action. We develop a principled, verifiable semantic communication method using a random-support Dirichlet--Categorical model of inductive logical probability, providing a modern statistical reinterpretation of Carnap's and Hintikka's systems. From this model, we derive a goal-oriented semantic information-bottleneck formulation that prioritizes evidence transmission by its reduction of uncertainty over task goals. Using 152 traffic rules extracted from the California Driver Handbook, we evaluate the framework on MDrive simulator in CARLA. Under identical communication budgets, semantic evidence selection completes every scenario without safety hazards, whereas uniform evidence selection produces collisions, showcasing semantic communication's superiority.
tldr: This paper proposes a goal-oriented semantic communication framework using first-order logic and neuro-symbolic reasoning for autonomous driving, focusing on efficient transmission of traffic rule evidence.
motivation: To enable reliable and efficient communication among connected autonomous vehicles and roadside units for safe decision-making under limited bandwidth.
method: The method uses a Dirichlet-Categorical model of inductive logical probability to derive a semantic information-bottleneck that selects the most informative observations for traffic rule evaluation, and employs LLM agents for action selection.
result: In CARLA simulations, the semantic selection method avoids all safety hazards under communication budgets, whereas uniform selection leads to collisions.
conclusion: Semantic communication with goal-oriented evidence selection can significantly improve safety in collaborative autonomous driving compared to uniform transmission.

title: Skillsets On The Chain: A Blockchain-based Zero-Trust Framework For Agentic Ai Networking
authors: Yayu Gao, Yong Xiao, Hao Hu, Xubo Li, Zhiwei Liu, Yingyu Li, Guangming Shi, Ping Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agentic AI networking (AgentNet) systems rely heavily on third-party skillset implementations and distributed multi-agent collaboration, yet they face major claim-to-capability inconsistencies and security vulnerabilities under trust-by-declaration assumptions. To bridge this gap, this paper proposes TrustAgentNet, a dual-tier blockchain-secured zero-trust framework. Specifically, a global Chain of Skillsets (CoS) governs the lifecycle of skillset metadata with protocols empowered by specialized agents to enforce off-chain auditing while maintaining lightweight on-chain cryptographic consensus. Furthermore, transient, task-oriented Chains of Collaboration (CoC) are dynamically established to enable trustless distributed multi-agent collaboration. Theoretical analysis of the three-way trade-off among security level, task performance, and resource overhead is provided and empirically validated. Experimental results on a hardware prototype demonstrate that compared with no-blockchain trust-by-default baselines, the zero-trust overhead of TrustAgentNet is dominated by off-chain inference, while the blockchain layer incurs minor ledger costs via the ledger-IPFS storage and on/off-chain integration design. Crucially, the proposed verification pipeline achieves a flawless 100% accuracy across 50 AI models, correctly validating 40 honest skillsets and intercepting 10 adversarial ones, and generalizes to non-AI domains with an 83.91% accuracy and a 0.85 F1-score across 1478 features from 171 ClawHub skills. Adversarial experiments further show that TrustAgentNet enables autonomous skillset self-recovery against various malicious attacks.
tldr: This paper proposes a blockchain-based zero-trust framework for agentic AI networking, focusing on security and trust management rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Agentic AI networking systems suffer from trust-by-declaration vulnerabilities and claim-to-capability inconsistencies, necessitating a secure framework.
method: The authors introduce TrustAgentNet, a dual-tier blockchain-secured zero-trust framework with a global Chain of Skillsets (CoS) for metadata governance and transient Chains of Collaboration (CoC) for distributed multi-agent collaboration, incorporating off-chain auditing and on-chain consensus.
result: The framework achieves 100% accuracy in validating honest and adversarial AI models, with low blockchain overhead, and generalizes to non-AI domains with 83.91% accuracy and 0.85 F1-score.
conclusion: The proposed framework effectively enhances security and trust in agentic AI networking, with minimal overhead, but is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Deep Learning For Cyber Threat Detection And Mitigation In Healthcare-IoT
authors: Mirza Akhi
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00118v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cybersecurity is a fundamental requirement for protecting wearable devices used in healthcare Internet of Things (H-IoT) systems. Security failures in these resource-constrained systems directly compromise patient safety. Physiological data and network traffic are frequent targets of cyberattacks in H-IoT environments. To address these risks, deep learning-based cybersecurity mechanisms for H-IoT often involve complex architectures with large parameter counts. Existing datasets are also rarely assessed for quality, limiting their applicability. However, this research addresses these challenges by developing multiple realistic datasets and proposing lightweight deep learning models, namely the Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) and Residual TCN (Res-TCN), for H-IoT. It includes two binary classification datasets for Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks and a multiclass dataset representing Selective Forwarding (SF), Man-in-the-Middle (MITM), and DDoS attacks. The datasets UL-ECE-MQTT-DDoS-H-IoT2025 and UL-ECE-UDP-DDoS-H-IoT2025 are generated in Cooja and ns-3 to capture transmission behaviours and protocol variations. The third dataset, UL-ECE-MultiAttack-H-IoT2025, integrates physiological and network features to represent multiple cyber threats in H-IoT. Building on this, the TCN model is designed to detect and mitigate DDoS attacks over the MQTT and UDP-based datasets. It incorporates a monitoring frequency-based detection mechanism and a dynamic threshold-based mitigation strategy. To enable edge deployment, the model is quantised and converted into TensorFlow Lite (TFLite) for real-time DDoS detection on Raspberry Pi 4, achieving low latency and power-efficient operation in H-IoT. This thesis establishes a deep learning-based cybersecurity defence mechanism encompassing realistic dataset generation, lightweight model design, and edge deployment for securing H-IoT systems.
tldr: This paper develops lightweight deep learning models (TCN and Res-TCN) for detecting and mitigating cyberattacks in healthcare IoT systems, including dataset generation and edge deployment.
motivation: Healthcare IoT devices are vulnerable to cyberattacks, and existing deep learning solutions are often too complex for resource-constrained devices. The research aims to create realistic datasets and lightweight models for effective and efficient threat detection.
method: The authors generate three datasets (two binary for DDoS, one multiclass for SF, MITM, DDoS) using Cooja and ns-3 simulators, then design TCN and Res-TCN models with monitoring frequency-based detection and dynamic threshold-based mitigation. The models are quantized and converted to TensorFlow Lite for deployment on Raspberry Pi 4.
result: The proposed models achieve low latency and power-efficient operation on edge devices, demonstrating effective DDoS detection and mitigation in H-IoT environments.
conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive cybersecurity framework for H-IoT, combining realistic dataset generation, lightweight model design, and edge deployment, but it is not aligned with the specified research directions in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Understanding Federated Learning Through The Lens Of Mechanism Design: The Role Of Data Heterogeneity
authors: Lina Alkarmi, Po-Yen Chen, Mingyan Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Federated learning (FL) requires effective incentive mechanisms to motivate data sharing and prevent strategic free-riding. Recent FL mechanisms such as the Shapley value mechanism M^Shap guarantee reciprocal fairness for agents. However, a complete analysis of how such mechanisms impact social optimality and individual rationality under realistic, standalone outside options remains unknown. In this paper, we address this gap by adapting the classical Externality mechanism M^E to the federated learning setting. We conduct a comparison of M^Shap and M^E across three dimensions: social optimality, individual rationality, and fairness/reciprocity. First, we establish that M^Shap generally does not maximize social welfare because its marginal incentives drive agents to over-contribute resources, while M^E maximizes social welfare by design. Second, we evaluate participation incentives through the individual rationality gap when considering agents' outside options as standalone training on their own data. We find that both mechanisms ensure individual rationality in homogeneous settings. We further show that under mild conditions, M^E maintains this guarantee under agent heterogeneity, whereas M^Shap does not. Third, we demonstrate that while M^Shap maintains perfect reciprocity by design, M^E generally does not, and only ensures that individual benefits match Shapley contributions at symmetric equilibria under homogeneity, as it sacrifices individual fairness to maximize collective welfare under heterogeneity. Empirical simulations validate our theoretical findings and illustrate a tradeoff between reciprocal fairness and social efficiency.
tldr: This paper analyzes federated learning incentive mechanisms through mechanism design, focusing on data heterogeneity, but does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper addresses the lack of analysis of incentive mechanisms in federated learning under realistic outside options and data heterogeneity.
method: The authors adapt the classical Externality mechanism to federated learning and compare it with the Shapley value mechanism across social optimality, individual rationality, and fairness.
result: They find that the Shapley mechanism does not maximize social welfare, while the Externality mechanism does, but the latter sacrifices individual fairness under heterogeneity.
conclusion: The paper highlights a tradeoff between reciprocal fairness and social efficiency in federated learning, but it is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Trimming: Decoupling Multiplicative Depth From Modulus Chains In Rns-ckks Via Rational Levels
authors: John Chiang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00375v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent work on Grafting decouples scale factors from ciphertext moduli, enabling more flexible precision management in RNS-CKKS. However, the multiplicative depth remains fundamentally constrained by the modulus chain structure. In this paper, we propose , a novel fine-grained level management mechanism that decouples multiplicative depth from modulus chains in RNS-CKKS via rational levels. The key idea is to introduce an auxiliary trimming modulus chain composed of smaller NTT-friendly modulus factors, which enables partial modulus transitions instead of directly discarding an entire modulus factor. By replacing conventional discrete level reductions with fine-grained modulus factor refinement, Trimming provides a rational-level abstraction beyond the traditional integer-based modulus chain representation. Our approach preserves the compatibility with existing RNS-CKKS arithmetic while enabling more flexible depth management and adaptive modulus transitions. Similar to Grafting, which addresses the precision bottleneck, Trimming targets the depth bottleneck in RNS-CKKS and contributes toward a fully decoupled RNS-CKKS architecture. The proposed framework will be further validated through concrete implementation and experimental evaluation to investigate its practical performance and computational overhead in real-world homomorphic encryption applications.
tldr: This paper proposes a fine-grained level management mechanism for RNS-CKKS homomorphic encryption to decouple multiplicative depth from modulus chains.
motivation: The paper aims to address the depth bottleneck in RNS-CKKS, which limits the number of consecutive multiplications in homomorphic encryption.
method: It introduces an auxiliary trimming modulus chain with smaller NTT-friendly factors to enable partial modulus transitions, providing a rational-level abstraction.
result: The proposed framework is expected to enable more flexible depth management and adaptive modulus transitions, but concrete implementation and experimental evaluation are not yet provided.
conclusion: The work contributes to a fully decoupled RNS-CKKS architecture, but its practical performance remains to be validated.

title: TI-StegoAlign: Channel-Guided Post-Training For Generative Text Steganography Under Tokenization Inconsistency
authors: Jiuan Zhou, Yuhao Xue, Yu Cheng, Yuan Xie, Zhaoxia Yin
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative text steganography enables LLM agents to exchange secret information through task-relevant messages. Yet most methods evaluate recovery on sender-side tokens, whereas the receiver observes only surface text. Detokenization and receiver-side retokenization can alter token boundaries, desynchronize coding states, and cause such evaluation to overestimate receiver-side recovery. Existing remedies rely on inference-time filtering or verification, correcting individual outputs without adapting the generation policy to the receiver-side channel. To address these limitations, we propose TI-StegoAlign, a channel-guided post-training framework. The Bit-Consistent Supervised Objective (BCSO) enlarges local coding margins at realized sender-side embedding positions. Channel-Conditioned Preference Optimization (CCPO) then aligns complete stegotexts using receiver-realistic recovery, text quality, and anti-steganalysis feedback. TI-StegoAlign updates only LoRA parameters and requires no tokenization-specific correction during communication. Experimental results show 100% receiver bit accuracy. Compared with the strongest baselines, TI-StegoAlign achieves a 21.6% reduction in normalized perplexity deviation and a 6.3% relative improvement in anti-steganalysis performance.
tldr: This paper proposes a post-training framework for generative text steganography to improve receiver-side bit recovery under tokenization inconsistency.
motivation: Existing generative text steganography methods often evaluate recovery on sender-side tokens, but receiver-side detokenization and retokenization can cause token boundary mismatches, leading to overestimated recovery. Current remedies are inference-time and do not adapt the generation policy to the receiver-side channel.
method: The authors introduce TI-StegoAlign, a channel-guided post-training framework with two components: Bit-Consistent Supervised Objective (BCSO) to enlarge local coding margins at sender-side embedding positions, and Channel-Conditioned Preference Optimization (CCPO) to align stegotexts using receiver-realistic recovery, text quality, and anti-steganalysis feedback. Only LoRA parameters are updated.
result: Experiments show 100% receiver bit accuracy, a 21.6% reduction in normalized perplexity deviation, and a 6.3% relative improvement in anti-steganalysis performance compared to baselines.
conclusion: The proposed framework effectively addresses tokenization inconsistency in generative text steganography, improving receiver-side recovery without requiring tokenization-specific corrections during communication.

title: Adversarial Attacks In Multi-Agent Llm Pipelines: Unveiling Structural Vulnerabilities In Agentic Ai Architectures
authors: Faisal Haque Bappy, Tahrim Hossain, Tarannum Shaila Zaman, Raiful Hasan, Kamrul Hasan, Tariqul Islam
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00718v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent LLM pipelines orchestrate multiple specialized language model agents into structured workflows where intermediate outputs are passed across agents to solve complex tasks. This design introduces a security gap absent in single-agent settings: once an agent accepts adversarial content, it is propagated as trusted input throughout the pipeline. We argue that this vulnerability stems from the absence of boundary verification, a security primitive that enforces explicit validation of data as it crosses inter-agent boundaries, including content, identity, execution intent, and state integrity. Without such verification, modern pipelines embed implicit trust assumptions that are not adversarially robust, giving rise to structurally distinct attack surfaces (e.g., content injection, agent impersonation, plan deviation, and memory poisoning). Leveraging annotated production traces from the GAIA and SWE-Bench benchmark, we show that these vulnerabilities arise in benign deployments and largely evade existing evaluation frameworks. We further operationalize these failure modes within a controlled multi-agent setting and evaluate them across GPT-5-mini, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and Kimi K2.5 under identical pipeline configurations. The results reveal that attack success aligns with pipeline structure rather than model capability, indicating that adversarial vulnerability is fundamentally an architectural property and motivating a shift toward pipeline-level defenses.
tldr: This paper analyzes adversarial attacks in multi-agent LLM pipelines, identifying structural vulnerabilities due to lack of boundary verification.
motivation: Multi-agent LLM pipelines introduce security gaps absent in single-agent settings, as adversarial content can propagate as trusted input across agents.
method: The authors use annotated production traces from GAIA and SWE-Bench to show vulnerabilities, and operationalize failure modes in a controlled multi-agent setting, evaluating across GPT-5-mini, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and Kimi K2.5.
result: Attack success aligns with pipeline structure rather than model capability, indicating adversarial vulnerability is an architectural property.
conclusion: The findings motivate a shift toward pipeline-level defenses, emphasizing the need for boundary verification in agentic AI architectures.

title: Safety Invariants For Agents Orchestrating Irreversible State Transitions: A Four-Dimensional Formalism Evaluated On Public Ledgers
authors: Zhaoming Yin
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00783v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous agents are increasingly asked to produce irreversible effects on external systems - transferring funds, writing to durable storage, actuating hardware. Existing agent frameworks (ReAct, Reflexion, MCP) optimize task success on benchmarks and give little attention to the safety of irreversible side-effects. We formalize one such setting, movement of value across public ledgers, as state transitions in a four-dimensional space indexed by (wallet, chain, address, protocol), and use that formalism to state and prove a guarantee we call execution fidelity: under a fault model admitting planner mis-mapping, ambiguous outcomes, retries, at-least-once delivery, and delegated non-human callers, a session's realized effect on the ledger is either nothing at all or exactly the transition that was rendered to the user, exactly once. The theorem deliberately does not claim that the rendered transition matches the user's intent - no runtime layer can decide that - but it confines that unbounded question to a single predicate over a finite object, which is what makes a preview a sufficient control rather than a formality. Seven safety invariants, derived from the fidelity condition rather than enumerated from experience, discharge the guarantee. Empirically, on a controlled N=60 adversarial suite the stack lifts pass rate by ~74 percentage points over a naive-ReAct baseline on two write-aggressive backing models, but by only ~3 points on a write-cautious one - evidence that single-model evaluations of agent safety stacks are close to unfalsifiable. The system is deployed; 108 production write operations across 8 chains back the failure taxonomy. Although the evaluation setting is public ledgers, the formalism and invariants apply to any probabilistic agent acting on irreversible external state.
tldr: This paper formalizes safety invariants for agents performing irreversible state transitions on public ledgers, proving execution fidelity under a fault model.
motivation: Existing agent frameworks optimize task success but neglect safety of irreversible side-effects, motivating a formal approach to guarantee correct execution.
method: The authors model ledger value movement as state transitions in a four-dimensional space and derive seven safety invariants from a fidelity condition, then evaluate on an adversarial suite.
result: The stack improves pass rate by ~74 points on write-aggressive models but only ~3 on a write-cautious one, with 108 production operations supporting the taxonomy.
conclusion: The formalism and invariants apply broadly to probabilistic agents acting on irreversible external state, but the paper is not aligned with the user's quantum information research interests.

title: Block Sensitivity Can Exceed Spectral Sensitivity Squared
authors: Alexander Meiburg
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The spectral sensitivity [MATH] of a Boolean function is the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix of its sensitivity graph. It lower-bounds every standard measure of query complexity, and Aaronson, Ben-David, Kothari, Rao and Tal, who introduced it, asked whether block sensitivity is at most quadratic in it: is [MATH]? We show that it is not. We construct a total Boolean function on [MATH] variables with [MATH] and [MATH], so that [MATH], and hence by composition a family with [MATH] and [MATH]. The function is the indicator of a union of [MATH] subcubes indexed by the vertices of a doubly regular tournament, and the freedom left in the construction is fixed by the Lov\'asz local lemma. The main result has been formally verified in Lean. We also give numerical evidence that a member of the same family on [MATH] variables reaches an exponent near [MATH], and exhibit a member on [MATH] variables whose exponent already exceeds [MATH] and whose spectral sensitivity can be computed exactly.
tldr: This paper disproves a conjecture about the relationship between block sensitivity and spectral sensitivity of Boolean functions, a result in classical computational complexity.
motivation: The paper addresses an open question in Boolean function complexity theory, specifically whether block sensitivity is at most quadratic in spectral sensitivity, which has implications for query complexity lower bounds.
method: The authors construct a total Boolean function based on a union of subcubes indexed by a doubly regular tournament, using the Lovász local lemma to fix parameters, and verify the main result in the Lean proof assistant.
result: They show that block sensitivity can exceed spectral sensitivity squared, providing a counterexample to the conjecture and a family of functions with a larger exponent.
conclusion: The result refutes the quadratic relationship, indicating that spectral sensitivity does not tightly bound block sensitivity, which may impact the understanding of query complexity measures.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Participation Governance For Verifiable Ai Agents In Open Digital Twin Ecosystems
authors: Juan Li, Wei Cai, Yan Bai
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous AI agents, increasingly empowered by large language models, are becoming important components of human-machine systems for high-stakes decision support in digital twin ecosystems. However, existing multi-agent systems often lack robust verification for identity, capability, and policy compliance, especially in decentralized environments spanning multiple institutions. This paper proposes a neuro-symbolic decentralized governance framework for verifiable agents in collaborative digital twin environments. By representing agents through multi-layer semantic profiles, the framework bridges probabilistic neural reasoning with deterministic institutional governance, thereby supporting trustworthy human-AI collaboration and meaningful human oversight. Capabilities are grounded in formal domain ontologies to enable machine-interpretable, policy-aware, and context-sensitive participation. These credentials, issued by organizational authorities, are validated via blockchain-based smart contracts, ensuring auditable participation without exposing sensitive data. We demonstrate the framework using a decision-support prototype with clinic, digital twin, and wearable provider agents effectively prevents unauthorized interaction and enforces institutional policies with manageable overhead. Our findings suggest that neuro-symbolic decentralized governance provides a scalable and trustworthy pathway for safe human-machine collaboration across institutional boundaries.
tldr: This paper proposes a neuro-symbolic decentralized governance framework for verifiable AI agents in digital twin ecosystems, using semantic profiles and blockchain-based credentials.
motivation: Existing multi-agent systems lack robust verification for identity, capability, and policy compliance in decentralized environments, hindering trustworthy human-AI collaboration.
method: The framework represents agents via multi-layer semantic profiles grounded in domain ontologies, and validates credentials through blockchain-based smart contracts.
result: A decision-support prototype with clinic, digital twin, and wearable provider agents prevents unauthorized interaction and enforces institutional policies with manageable overhead.
conclusion: Neuro-symbolic decentralized governance offers a scalable and trustworthy pathway for safe human-machine collaboration across institutional boundaries.

title: NoisePQC++: A Unified NIST-Compliant Pqc And Hybrid-PQC Implementation Of The Noise Protocol
authors: Nadeem Ahmed, Aryya Gangopadhyay, Lei Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The threat of quantum computers to classical public-key cryptography has created an urgent need to evolve secure communication protocols with post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) primitives. The Noise Protocol Framework, widely used in systems such as WireGuard and WhatsApp, traditionally relies on the Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) public-key exchange scheme, which is vulnerable to quantum threats. In this paper, we present NoisePQC++, a unified C++23 implementation of the Noise Protocol framework augmented with post-quantum Key Encapsulation Mechanisms and Hybrid Forward Secrecy. Our design integrates the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) standardized ML-KEM algorithm alongside classical ECDH, enabling full PQC, hybrid ECDH+PQC handshakes, and unified support for all 57 classical Noise handshake pattern variants, 13 post-quantum Noise handshakes, and their hybrid variants. Compared with prior work, NoisePQC++ offers broader protocol coverage, more complete implementation support, and greater flexibility. Our evaluation shows minimal overhead under normal network conditions and acceptable overhead in adverse cases, while significantly improving resistance against quantum adversaries. These results indicate that NIST-standardized post-quantum and hybrid Noise handshakes are practical and provide a credible basis for future deployment.
tldr: This paper presents a C++ implementation of the Noise Protocol Framework with post-quantum and hybrid key exchange, but it is primarily a software engineering effort with no new information-theoretic or physical insights.
motivation: The threat of quantum computers to classical public-key cryptography motivates integrating NIST-standardized post-quantum algorithms into secure communication protocols like the Noise Protocol Framework.
method: The authors implement NoisePQC++, a C++23 library that integrates ML-KEM with classical ECDH, supporting all 57 classical Noise handshake patterns, 13 post-quantum handshakes, and hybrid variants.
result: The implementation shows minimal overhead under normal network conditions and acceptable overhead in adverse cases, while improving resistance against quantum adversaries.
conclusion: The paper concludes that NIST-standardized post-quantum and hybrid Noise handshakes are practical and provide a credible basis for future deployment.

title: Truncated Differentiation For Inverse Potential MFGs
authors: Siting Liu, Yat Tin Chow, Samy Wu Fung
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00217v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study inverse potential mean-field games (MFGs), in which an unknown spatial inverse-cost (mobility) map is inferred from observed population densities. We solve the forward MFG with a preconditioned primal-dual hybrid gradient (PDHG) method and develop Jacobian-free backpropagation (JFB-[MATH]), which records only the final [MATH] iterations from a detached warm start while retaining the full forward solve. To analyze this truncated differentiation method, we show that the exact-proximal dual-extrapolated PDHG map is a metric resolvent of the maximal monotone KKT operator. This resolvent view shows that JFB-[MATH] exactly differentiates a finite-trajectory surrogate and, under a locally fixed active set at an exact equilibrium detach point, converges to the implicit gradient as the tracked depth increases. Across several inverse-MFG settings, numerical experiments show that JFB-r at moderate tracked depths can achieve recovery accuracy comparable to full unrolling while reducing memory and runtime.
tldr: This paper develops a truncated differentiation method for solving inverse potential mean-field games, focusing on computational efficiency in optimization.
motivation: The authors aim to efficiently infer unknown spatial mobility maps in mean-field games, which is a challenging inverse problem with high computational cost.
method: They propose Jacobian-free backpropagation with truncated differentiation (JFB-r) that records only the final iterations from a detached warm start, and analyze it via metric resolvent theory of the KKT operator.
result: Numerical experiments show that JFB-r achieves comparable recovery accuracy to full unrolling while reducing memory and runtime.
conclusion: The truncated differentiation method offers a practical trade-off between accuracy and computational resources for inverse MFGs.

title: Robust Watermarks Meet Backdoored Models: Evading Diffusion Semantic Watermarks Via Stealthy Backdoor
authors: Jinyuan Liu, Tianshuo Cong, Pei Li, Tianrui Wang, Xinlei He, Anyu Wang, Xiaoyun Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00543v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Although semantic watermarking is considered a promising safeguard for images generated by Latent Diffusion Models (LDMs), the reliance of the watermark detection pipeline on neural networks introduces a critical yet underexplored backdoor attack surface. To systematically study this vulnerability, we propose GhostVAE to plant a stealthy backdoor into the encoder of Variational Autoencoder (VAE), enabling reliable evasion of watermark detection. GhostVAE operates in two stages: it first constructs a universal trigger via power spectrum regularization to improve the trigger robustness, and then trains a backdoored VAE encoder with a parameter-aligned objective. Through extensive evaluations across three state-of-the-art semantic watermarking schemes and three widely adopted LDMs, we show that GhostVAE preserves watermark detection performance on benign images (achieving an average true positive rate of 94.4%), while simultaneously enabling highly effective evasion under trigger activation (achieving an average attack success rate of 94.6%). Moreover, we comprehensively analyze seventeen representative defenses and demonstrate that GhostVAE remains stealthy across the input space, parameter space, and latent space. Our work fundamentally undermines the trustworthiness of semantic watermarking systems and highlights that secure deployment of semantic watermarks requires end-to-end security considerations, particularly for neural network components.
tldr: This paper introduces GhostVAE, a backdoor attack on the VAE encoder of latent diffusion models to evade semantic watermark detection.
motivation: Semantic watermarking for AI-generated images relies on neural networks, which are vulnerable to backdoor attacks, threatening the trustworthiness of such safeguards.
method: GhostVAE constructs a universal trigger via power spectrum regularization and trains a backdoored VAE encoder with a parameter-aligned objective to evade watermark detection.
result: GhostVAE preserves watermark detection on benign images (94.4% true positive rate) while achieving 94.6% attack success rate under trigger activation, and remains stealthy against 17 defenses.
conclusion: The work highlights that secure deployment of semantic watermarks requires end-to-end security considerations, as neural network components can be compromised.

title: Explainable Hybrid Feature Selection For Intrusion Detection In Internet Of Medical Things Environments
authors: Amira Berrezzek, Hayet Djellali, Giulio Mallardi, Lamia Mahnane
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00869v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) networks are hard to protect: devices are heterogeneous, computing resources are scarce, and traffic must be analyzed in real time. We present an intrusion detection system that addresses these constraints through feature selection. A Pearson correlation filter first removes redundant attributes; a hybrid strategy then combines model-based feature importance with SHAP attribution to pick a compact subset, on which we train Random Forest and LightGBM classifiers. SHAP and LIME explain what each retained feature contributes to the decisions. On CIC-IoMT 2024 and CIC-IDS 2017, the method cuts the feature space by up to 88% - from 40 to as few as 5 features - and accuracy and F1-score stay within a few points of models trained on all features. Compact, interpretable detectors of this kind are practical candidates for deployment on resource-limited medical networks.
tldr: This paper presents an intrusion detection system for IoMT networks using hybrid feature selection with SHAP and LIME explanations.
motivation: IoMT networks are heterogeneous and resource-constrained, requiring efficient and interpretable intrusion detection.
method: The method combines Pearson correlation filtering, model-based feature importance, and SHAP attribution to select a compact feature subset, then trains Random Forest and LightGBM classifiers with SHAP and LIME for explanation.
result: On CIC-IoMT 2024 and CIC-IDS 2017, the method reduces features by up to 88% while maintaining accuracy and F1-score within a few points of full-feature models.
conclusion: Compact, interpretable detectors are practical for deployment on resource-limited medical networks.

title: Sub-40 Nm Resolution Deep Tissue Imaging By Image Scanning Emission Saturation Nanoscopy
authors: Chenyi Wang, Tiange Zhang, Chaohao Chen, Xuchen Shan, Meiqi Li, Xiaolan Zhong, Fan Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00456v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The development of deep-tissue super-resolution imaging serves as an essential bridge toward non-invasive in vivo optical observation. However, there remain challenges to balance spatial resolution, imaging depth and phototoxicity. Here, we present a nanoscopy namely Image Scanning Emission Saturation (ISES) nanoscopy, achieving a lateral resolution of 37 nm, 1/25th of the excitation wavelength, at an imaging depth of 200 {\mu}m. Using a 976-nm doughnut-shaped excitation beam within an imaging-scanning microscopy configuration, we apply saturation-based point spread function (PSF) engineering and pixel-level confocal-pinhole enhancement to improve spatial resolution. As the high- and low-frequency components of the image OTF are concurrently acquired in a single scan via different camera pixels, Fourier-domain fusion can be employed with a single scanning dataset to further improve image quality. Compared with the traditional doughnut excitation beam-based adaptive pixel reassignment method, our strategy preserves the original frequency distributions and mitigates reconstruction artifacts in complex biological sample imaging. This strategy is generalizable and compatible with a variety of probes displaying saturation behavior. Beyond enabling a versatile and practical approach for deep tissue super-resolution imaging, it also informs the development of next-generation nanoprobes for imaging.
tldr: This paper presents a deep-tissue super-resolution imaging technique using saturation-based point spread function engineering, achieving 37 nm resolution at 200 μm depth.
motivation: The goal is to develop non-invasive deep-tissue super-resolution imaging that balances resolution, depth, and phototoxicity.
method: The method combines image scanning microscopy with a doughnut-shaped excitation beam to induce emission saturation, and uses pixel-level confocal-pinhole enhancement and Fourier-domain fusion to improve resolution.
result: The technique achieves a lateral resolution of 37 nm (1/25th of excitation wavelength) at 200 μm depth, and reduces reconstruction artifacts compared to traditional methods.
conclusion: The approach is generalizable and compatible with various probes, offering a practical solution for deep-tissue super-resolution imaging and informing nanoprobe development.

title: Renormalizations In Holomorphic Field Theories On K\"ahler Manifolds
authors: Junrong Yan Minghao Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The divergence of Feynman graph integrals is one of the central issues in the study of perturbative quantum field theories. A rigorous formulation of these integrals usually requires renormalization. In this paper, we prove that the Feynman graph integrals arising from holomorphic field theories on closed real-analytic K\"ahler manifolds are convergent with respect to heat-kernel renormalization, Cauchy principal value renormalization, and zeta-function renormalization. Moreover, these three renormalization procedures produce the same value. Our proof is based on the theory of wonderful compactifications in algebraic geometry, which provides a geometric understanding of these integrals. As a consequence, we establish a gauge anomaly formula for these graph integrals.
tldr: This paper proves convergence and equality of three renormalization schemes for Feynman graph integrals in holomorphic field theories on Kähler manifolds, using wonderful compactifications.
motivation: The paper addresses the mathematical problem of rigorously defining Feynman graph integrals in perturbative quantum field theory, which often diverge and require renormalization.
method: The authors use the theory of wonderful compactifications from algebraic geometry to provide a geometric framework for analyzing the integrals, and then prove convergence for heat-kernel, Cauchy principal value, and zeta-function renormalizations.
result: They show that the Feynman graph integrals are convergent under all three renormalization procedures and that the results coincide, and they derive a gauge anomaly formula.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous mathematical foundation for these integrals, but it is not connected to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Spectroscopy Of The Hyperfine Structure Of Hd$^+$ In Rotationally Excited States With 10-ppb Uncertainty
authors: D. Kliukin, V. Barb\'e, T. Klijn Velderman, J. B. E. Schokking, J. John, K. S. E. Eikema, J. C. J. Koelemeij, J. -Ph. Karr
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00607v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report the first measurement of the total hyperfine interval in the manifold of the ([MATH]) rovibrational state of HD[MATH] using microwave spectroscopy of HD[MATH] ions in a linear Paul trap. To overcome the low (0.2%) occupancy of the quantum states involved, we employ a novel technique that combines intermittent Majorana depolarization of the HD[MATH] ensemble with redistribution of rotational-state population by blackbody radiation to effectively amplify the occupancy by a factor of 25. This enables the observation of a single field-insensitive magnetic subcomponent of the hyperfine transition, leading to a measured total hyperfine interval of [MATH]kHz with an unprecedented relative uncertainty of 10 parts per billion. This differs from the theoretically predicted value [MATH]kHz by 1.9[MATH]. We show that our experimental value is consistent with the recently measured hyperfine structure of the ([MATH]) rovibrational state of HD[MATH] [C.M. K\"onig et al., High-precision Penning trap spectroscopy of the ground state spin structure of HD[MATH], Phys. Rev. Lett. [MATH],143002 (2026)], for which a similar deviation from theory was found. Our work may help resolve puzzling discrepancies between the theoretical and experimental hyperfine structure observed previously in optical rovibrational spectra of HD[MATH].

method: The authors use microwave spectroscopy on HD+ ions in a linear Paul trap, employing intermittent Majorana depolarization and blackbody radiation to amplify the population of the target state.

title: Remarks On Regular Approximations To The Robin Aharonov-Bohm Hamiltonian
authors: Cesar R. de Oliveira
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In the space [MATH], for Robin parameter [MATH], it is shown that there is a family of Schr\"odinger operators with penetrable toroidal solenoid and variable conductivity that approximates the magnetic Aharonov-Bohm operator with a Robin boundary condition at the solenoid (border). It is also shown that approximations via smooth potentials and then a barrier in the solenoid interior give Dirichlet boundary conditions. The approximations are in the strong resolvent sense and obtained through the [MATH]-convergence technique, and they hold for the more general setting of smooth, closed and compact surfaces and continuous and bounded magnetic potentials.
