title: Asymptotic Analysis Of Nonsymmetric Gaussian And Archimedean Compound Means
authors: Tomislav Buri\'c, Lenka Mihokovi\'c, Toni Milas
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies asymptotic expansions of the Gaussian and Archimedean compounds of two arbitrary bivariate means that need not be symmetric. Recursive algorithms for the coefficients of such expansions were previously obtained only in the symmetric case. Here, this restriction is removed and recursions are derived for the general nonsymmetric setting. All coefficient calculations are carried out in the algebra of formal power series. This introduces an additional case in the recursion, as well as singular configurations in which the formal invariance equation does not determine the coefficients recursively. The formal problem is kept separate from the existence and convergence of the iterative procedures. We also connect the first formal coefficients with Farhi's metric, recall its known global convergence criterion, and derive the corresponding local rates. The algorithms are illustrated using weighted power means and several known identities. Finally, the method is extended to expansions with sign-dependent coefficients and is applied to the neo-Pythagorean means and to a recently introduced two-parameter family.
tldr: This paper develops asymptotic expansions for nonsymmetric Gaussian and Archimedean compound means using formal power series, with applications to weighted power means and neo-Pythagorean means.
motivation: The paper aims to generalize previous recursive algorithms for symmetric compound means to the nonsymmetric case, addressing a gap in the mathematical literature.
method: The authors derive recursive algorithms for coefficients of asymptotic expansions in the algebra of formal power series, handling singular configurations and extending to sign-dependent coefficients.
result: They obtain recursions for the general nonsymmetric setting, connect first coefficients to Farhi's metric, and illustrate with examples including weighted power means and neo-Pythagorean means.
conclusion: The work extends the theory of compound means to nonsymmetric cases, providing tools for further analysis, but it is purely mathematical and unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Explicit Green's Functions And Adjoint Problems For Differential Equations With Linear Functional Perturbations
authors: Alberto Cabada, Paula Cambeses-Franco, Luc\'ia L\'opez-Somoza
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00092v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study a functional differential equation subject to two-point boundary value conditions, where the functional dependence is introduced through an operator of the form \sum_{k=1}^{l}\gamma_{k}(t)_{k}(u), where [MATH], [MATH], ([MATH]) are linear continuous operators and [MATH] for all [MATH]. This formulation encompasses, among others, equations with piecewise constant arguments and those with integral-type dependence. We analyze this class of equations by deducing and characterizing their Green's function, as well as by computing the related adjoint problem. This approach enables us to establish connections among different types of functional equations and to relate equations with piecewise constant arguments to impulsive differential equations and non local boundary value problems. Next, we develop a series of comparison principles and results that allow us to characterize the regions where the Green's function of the original problem and of its adjoint maintain a constant sign. Finally, we illustrate the theoretical finding with representative examples.
tldr: This paper studies functional differential equations with linear functional perturbations, deriving Green's functions and adjoint problems, which is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to analyze a class of functional differential equations with two-point boundary conditions, encompassing piecewise constant arguments and integral-type dependence, and to establish connections to impulsive and nonlocal problems.
method: The authors deduce and characterize Green's functions, compute adjoint problems, and develop comparison principles to determine sign regions.
result: They provide explicit Green's functions and adjoint problems, and characterize constant sign regions, illustrated with examples.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of functional differential equations but has no connection to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Residual Centering And Error Bounds For Convex Approximation Of Mixed-Integer Recourse
authors: Alban Kryeziu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study convex approximations of mixed-integer recourse functions in two-stage stochastic programming. For first-stage decisions, the relevant approximation error is the signed expected residual between the convex approximation and the integer-recourse value function. On bounded uncertainty boxes, we identify residual conditions that yield deterministic bounds for this expectation error. The central condition is coordinate slice-centering, under which integration by parts gives an anisotropic total-variation bound and a mixed-derivative bound whose all-coordinate case is expressed through Vitali variation of the density. Exact centering, however, may be incompatible with convexity, even for totally unimodular ceiling recourse. We therefore use commuting coordinate projectors to decompose an arbitrary residual into a centered component and an explicit slice-mean defect. The resulting defect-adjusted bounds provide selectable error certificates and uniform first-stage decision-quality guarantees. We further establish sharp constants, extend the mixed-derivative estimate to nonsmooth densities, and develop tensor-product and geometric extensions of the framework, alongside a max-affine convex fitting and audit methodology.
tldr: This paper studies convex approximations of mixed-integer recourse functions in two-stage stochastic programming, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper addresses error bounds for convex approximations in stochastic programming, a topic in operations research and optimization, with no connection to the user's research interests in quantum information theory.
method: The method involves residual centering, coordinate slice-centering, integration by parts, and total-variation bounds to derive deterministic error bounds for the approximation error.
result: The paper provides deterministic bounds for the expected residual error, including anisotropic total-variation and mixed-derivative bounds, and introduces defect-adjusted bounds for non-centered residuals.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theory of convex approximations in stochastic programming, but it is outside the scope of the user's research directions.

title: Commutants Of Composition Operators On Function Spaces Of Several Complex Variables
authors: Fr\'ed\'eric Bayart, Maofa Wang, Xingxing Yao
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is devoted to an in-depth study of the minimal commutant property for composition operators acting on Hilbert spaces of holomorphic functions in several complex variables, such as the Fock space on [MATH], the Hardy space on the Euclidean ball, and the Hardy space on the unit polydisc.
tldr: This paper studies the minimal commutant property for composition operators on Hilbert spaces of holomorphic functions in several complex variables, which is a topic in functional analysis and operator theory.
motivation: The paper aims to understand the algebraic structure of composition operators on function spaces, specifically the minimal commutant property, which is a classical question in operator theory.
method: The authors analyze composition operators on Fock, Hardy, and polydisc spaces, likely using techniques from complex analysis and operator theory to characterize when the commutant is minimal.

title: On The Iterate Convergence Of AdaGrad For Generalized Smooth Convex Optimization
authors: Tung Quoc Le Mathieu Besan\c{c}on
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00482v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove sequential convergence results for the AdaGrad algorithm family optimizing convex differentiable objectives. Specifically, we provide necessary and sufficient conditions for the convergence of iterates for the three main AdaGrad variants (AdaNorm, AdaDiag, AdaFull) when the objective is convex and locally Lipschitz-smooth, closing the question left open from the literature. We harness this general result to study the three variants under the generalized [MATH]-smoothness condition and show sequential convergence for sufficiently small constant step size. Moreover, under the so-called [MATH]-polynomially modifiable smoothness assumption, which is a relaxation of the [MATH] generalized smoothness property and is satisfied by many function classes such as [MATH]-smooth functions or univariate polynomials, sequential convergence for these AdaGrad variants is proved for arbitrary learning rates. This result provides conditions under which AdaGrad presents adaptivity, i.e., does not require tuning the parameters based on the instance. Finally, we provide numerical illustrations of the behavior of AdaGrad on convex and nonconvex functions. In particular, we construct a counterexample empirically showing that smoothness alone is not sufficient for the sequential convergence of AdaGrad-type algorithms, and suggesting that additional geometric hypotheses (e.g., convexity as in this paper, or the Kurdyka-\L ojasiewicz inequality) are indispensable for sequential convergence results.
tldr: This paper proves convergence results for AdaGrad optimization algorithms under generalized smoothness conditions, which is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper addresses open questions in the convergence of AdaGrad variants for convex optimization, a topic in machine learning and optimization theory.
method: The authors provide theoretical proofs of sequential convergence for AdaGrad variants under various smoothness assumptions, and supplement with numerical experiments.
result: They establish necessary and sufficient conditions for iterate convergence, and show convergence for generalized smoothness and polynomially modifiable smoothness, with a counterexample showing smoothness alone is insufficient.
conclusion: The work contributes to optimization theory but has no connection to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: From P\'olya's Conditions To A Complete Characterization Of The $l^2$ Convergence Of Hyperinterpolation
authors: Congpei An, Xiannan Hu, Xiaoming Yuan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It has remained open to identify the necessary and sufficient conditions for the [MATH] convergence of hyperinterpolation since it was introduced by Sloan in 1995. We show that the [MATH]-[MATH] Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund (MZ) condition, together with the asymptotic functional approximation property for polynomials, is the answer. We further prove that the optimal [MATH]-[MATH] MZ constant coincides with the operator norm of the hyperinterpolation operator, and it admits a natural Banach space duality interpretation. With an explicit construction, we also show that P\'{o}lya's classical conditions for quadrature convergence are not sufficient for the [MATH] convergence of hyperinterpolation. This reveals a fundamental distinction between the convergence of linear functionals (quadrature formulas) and that of linear operators (hyperinterpolation operators). We establish a strict logical hierarchy for the stability and accuracy conditions governing the convergence of quadrature and hyperinterpolation.
tldr: This paper characterizes the L2 convergence of hyperinterpolation, a numerical analysis topic, and is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper addresses an open problem in approximation theory regarding necessary and sufficient conditions for hyperinterpolation convergence.
method: The authors use Marcinkiewicz-Zygmund conditions and functional analysis to derive the characterization.
result: They prove that the MZ condition plus asymptotic functional approximation property is necessary and sufficient, and show Pólya's conditions are insufficient.
conclusion: The work clarifies the distinction between convergence of quadrature and hyperinterpolation, but has no connection to the user's research interests.

title: A Semi-implicit Double-point Material Point Method For Both Free-surface Flow And Seepage In Deformable Porous Media
authors: Mian Xie, Pedro Navas, Susana L\'opez-Querol
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00578v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A new semi-implicit, two-phase, double-point formulation of the Material Point Method (MPM) for soil-water interaction with seepage and free-surface flows under large deformation is presented in this paper. The approach advances the water phase implicitly while keeping the soil phase explicit, enabling stable, efficient time integration in problems that involve rapid seepage and strong free-surface motion. The proposed framework models high-Reynolds-number interphase drag through a non-linear Darcy's law implemented for the first time within an incremental fractional step MPM formulation without enlarging the implicit solve. This methodology also enhances the numerical stability for fast flows and wave breaking via a hyperelastic constitutive treatment of slightly compressible viscous water, and mitigates spurious oscillations through a new stabilisation approach for the velocity. Robustness of soil-water interface is achieved by combining nodal-based, free-surface detection, suited for higher-order spline functions with smooth porosity-permeability transitions that avoid constitutive divergence at sharp material boundaries. Validation against laboratory benchmark cases reported in the literature, including pure-water dam break, dam-break seepage through a porous barrier, two granular-collapse tsunami experiments, and a dam-break wave over a movable granular bed, shows accurate and stable free-surface evolution, pressure time histories, seepage fronts, and wave-gauge records. Using an advanced critical-state soil model (NorSand) further improves the reproduction of granular flow kinematics. The results demonstrate that the proposed formulation is a reliable and computationally efficient tool for geotechnical hazards involving intense soil-water coupling, seepage, sediment transport and free water.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical method (MPM) for simulating soil-water interaction, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The paper aims to improve simulation of geotechnical hazards involving soil-water coupling, seepage, and free-surface flows under large deformation.
method: It introduces a semi-implicit, two-phase, double-point Material Point Method (MPM) with implicit water phase and explicit soil phase, incorporating non-linear Darcy's law and hyperelastic water treatment.
result: Validation against laboratory benchmarks shows accurate and stable free-surface evolution, pressure histories, and seepage fronts.
conclusion: The proposed MPM formulation is a reliable and efficient tool for geotechnical engineering, but it has no connection to the user's research interests.

title: Study Of Landslides Through A Stabilised Semi-Implicit Material Point Method
authors: Mian Xie, Pedro Navas, Susana L\'opez-Querol
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00592v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this research, a new semi-implicit two-phase double-point material point method is proposed, in which the soil and water phases are modelled using two distinct sets of material points, both being stabilised with a novel approach. The Nor-Sand constitutive model is implemented to simulate more realistic soil behaviour. Some landslide numerical examples are presented to investigate the performance of the proposed method and highlight the importance of using the double-point approach. The formulation with two sets of material points shows significantly different but more reliable results in the cases of landslides, compared with the conventional single-point approach. Furthermore, this research shows that the additional computational cost given by the additional water material points is acceptable. Therefore, it is recommended to use two sets of material points for some large deformation geotechnical problems.
tldr: This paper proposes a stabilized semi-implicit two-phase double-point material point method for simulating landslides, which is a geotechnical engineering topic unrelated to quantum information.
motivation: The research aims to improve landslide simulations by modeling soil and water phases separately with a novel stabilization approach and a realistic constitutive model.
method: The method uses two sets of material points for soil and water, stabilized with a novel approach, and implements the Nor-Sand constitutive model within a semi-implicit double-point material point framework.
result: Numerical examples show that the double-point approach yields significantly different and more reliable results for landslides compared to the single-point approach, with acceptable additional computational cost.
conclusion: The authors recommend using two sets of material points for large deformation geotechnical problems like landslides.

title: Dynamic-Threshold Algorithms For The Continuous Quadratic Knapsack Problem: Reset Mechanisms And Complexity
authors: Yong-Jin Liu, Peicheng Xie, Chuan Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Condat's algorithm is an efficient dynamic-threshold method for projection onto the simplex, but its extension to weighted equality constraints and the algorithmic roles of resetting and removal have received limited analysis. We develop a dynamic-threshold algorithm (DTA) for a continuous quadratic knapsack problem with a weighted equality constraint. DTA maintains a threshold invariant through three operations--addition, reset, and removal--and we establish its finite termination and correctness. A sufficient condition under which reset cannot occur motivates a simpler no-reset variant, NDTA. We construct instances for which DTA runs in [MATH] time whereas NDTA requires [MATH] time, although both algorithms have quadratic worst-case complexity. We further show that, when the weight ratio and the number of deletions per removal pass are bounded, a linear number of passes with positive threshold increments requires the minimum nonzero gap between input values, normalized by the data range, to be at most [MATH]. Numerical experiments with up to 10^7 variables demonstrate that DTA and NDTA achieve approximately linear empirical scaling, and outperform Secant, WMVA, Variable Fixing, Newton, Median Search, Heap, and Sort in running time.
tldr: This paper presents dynamic-threshold algorithms for the continuous quadratic knapsack problem, a numerical optimization topic unrelated to quantum information.
motivation: The paper aims to improve algorithms for projection onto the simplex with weighted equality constraints, which is a classical optimization problem.
method: The authors develop a dynamic-threshold algorithm (DTA) with operations addition, reset, and removal, and a no-reset variant (NDTA), analyzing their complexity and termination.
result: They prove finite termination and correctness, show DTA can be faster than NDTA in certain instances, and demonstrate near-linear empirical scaling on large problems.
conclusion: The proposed algorithms are efficient for the continuous quadratic knapsack problem, but the topic is outside the user's research interests in quantum information and related areas.

title: Estimation Of Quantile Inequality Curves And Measures Based On Grouped Data
authors: Sylwester Pi\k{a}tek Alicja Jokiel-Rokita
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00766v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Estimation of quantile inequality curves and measures is considered in a parametric model based on grouped data. The unknown parameters of the distribution are estimated using the minimum divergence method, using various [MATH]-divergences. The consistency of the plug-in estimators of the inequality curves and measures and the asymptotic normality of the indices estimators are proved. In a simulation study, the methods are verified and compared in terms of the accuracy of the estimation. The practical applications of the proposed methods are illustrated by the analysis of two real data sets.
tldr: This paper proposes parametric estimation of quantile inequality curves and measures from grouped data using minimum divergence methods.
motivation: Quantile inequality measures are important in economics and social sciences, but estimation from grouped data is challenging.
method: The authors use minimum divergence estimation with various divergences to estimate distribution parameters from grouped data, then plug in to estimate inequality curves and measures.
result: They prove consistency and asymptotic normality of the estimators and validate via simulations and real data.
conclusion: The proposed methods provide accurate estimation of inequality measures from grouped data, with practical applications.

title: Concentration Theorems For $2$-homogeneous Polynomials And Bilinear Forms With Applications To The Kadec-Klee Properties
authors: Jorge Tom\'as Rodr\'iguez Sheldon Dantas
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Kadec-Klee properties in spaces of homogeneous polynomials and multilinear forms by presenting optimal results. Indeed, our main tool is a family of concentration theorems showing that, on suitable [MATH]-convex Banach sequence lattices, a [MATH]-homogeneous polynomial or a bilinear form which almost attains its norm at finitely supported vectors is uniformly close to its restriction to the corresponding finite set of coordinates. As a consequence, we obtain the weak-star uniform Kadec-Klee property for spaces of complex [MATH]-homogeneous polynomials and complex bilinear forms on [MATH]-convex Banach sequence lattices with constant one for some [MATH]. This applies, in particular, to [MATH], [MATH], Lorentz spaces [MATH], Garling spaces [MATH], among others. In the real setting, a concentration argument based on the modulus of convexity of power type yields further positive results for spaces of operators and bilinear forms, extending previous results in the literature. We also prove that the restriction [MATH] is optimal for [MATH]-homogeneous polynomials on [MATH], [MATH] and [MATH], and establish general failures of the sequential weak-star Kadec-Klee property for real homogeneous polynomials of degree at least two and for complex homogeneous polynomials and symmetric multilinear forms of degree at least three. These results show that our positive results are optimal respect to the degree and that the assumption [MATH] is optimal for the classical spaces [MATH], [MATH] and [MATH]. As a consequence of our results, we establish the strong subdifferentiability of the associated projective and symmetric projective tensor norms.
tldr: This paper studies Kadec-Klee properties in spaces of homogeneous polynomials and bilinear forms using concentration theorems, with applications to Banach space geometry.
motivation: The authors aim to characterize when spaces of polynomials and multilinear forms have the weak-star uniform Kadec-Klee property, a topic in Banach space theory.
method: They develop concentration theorems for 2-homogeneous polynomials and bilinear forms on certain Banach sequence lattices, and use modulus of convexity arguments for real spaces.
result: They obtain optimal results for Kadec-Klee properties in various spaces, including L_p, Lorentz, and Garling spaces, and establish optimality of the degree and assumptions.
conclusion: The paper contributes to the geometry of Banach spaces of polynomials, but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Weakly Normally Hyperbolic Invariant Tori: Persistence And An Averaging Principle
authors: Pedro C. C. R. Pereira Douglas D. Novaes
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00812v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a persistence theorem for attracting weakly normally hyperbolic invariant tori under small time-periodic perturbations. The theorem extends recent continuation results for weakly normally hyperbolic limit cycles to invariant tori of arbitrary dimension, providing a general analytical framework for their detection. As an application, we establish an averaging principle showing that attracting normally hyperbolic invariant [MATH]-tori of the averaged system give rise to attracting normally hyperbolic invariant [MATH]-tori of the original non-autonomous system. We further introduce a polynomiality-preserving construction that simultaneously lifts the dimensions of the phase space and the attracting normally hyperbolic invariant tori, yielding recursive lower bounds for the maximal number of codimension-[MATH] normally hyperbolic invariant tori of polynomial vector fields of a given degree, thereby extending the counting aspect of Hilbert's sixteenth problem to higher-dimensional invariant tori. In particular, we prove that this number grows at least polynomially with the degree and becomes unbounded for invariant tori of higher codimension.
tldr: This paper proves a persistence theorem for weakly normally hyperbolic invariant tori under periodic perturbations and establishes an averaging principle, with applications to counting invariant tori in polynomial vector fields.
motivation: The paper aims to extend recent results on weakly normally hyperbolic limit cycles to higher-dimensional invariant tori, providing a general framework for their detection and persistence.
method: The authors develop a persistence theorem for attracting weakly normally hyperbolic invariant tori under small time-periodic perturbations, and use it to establish an averaging principle. They also introduce a polynomiality-preserving construction to lift dimensions and derive recursive lower bounds for the number of invariant tori.
result: The main results include a persistence theorem, an averaging principle, and lower bounds for the maximal number of codimension-k normally hyperbolic invariant tori of polynomial vector fields, showing polynomial growth with degree.
conclusion: The paper contributes to dynamical systems theory, extending the counting aspect of Hilbert's sixteenth problem to higher-dimensional invariant tori, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: A Helmholtz-Leray Projection Method With Variational Multiscale Stabilization For The Navier-Stokes Equations
authors: Biswajit Khara, Suresh Murugaiyan, Makrand Khanwale, Baskar Ganapathysubramanian
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00843v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Galerkin finite element formulation of the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations presents two principal challenges: maintaining stable velocity-pressure coupling and controlling instability in advection-dominated regimes. Moreover, the monolithic formulation produces a coupled nonlinear saddle-point problem. In this work, we present a residual-based variational multiscale (VMS) stabilization of an incremental Helmholtz-Leray projection method that replaces this coupled saddle-point problem with a nonlinear velocity predictor, a pressure Poisson equation, and a velocity projection. The multiscale decomposition is applied only to the predicted velocity; neither the pressure nor the corrected, weakly divergence-free velocity is decomposed into coarse and fine scales. The modeled velocity fine scale contributes consistently to all three subproblems, introducing SUPG-like stabilization in the momentum predictor and a PSPG-like residual contribution in the pressure Poisson equation. We provide a formal error decomposition that separates the BDF2 time-discretization, projection-splitting, and spatial-VMS errors and, under stated stability and spatial-approximation assumptions, yields a combined velocity error estimate with second-order temporal accuracy. Numerical results for manufactured solutions, lid-driven cavity flow, flow past a cylinder, and the Taylor-Green vortex agree closely with established reference data. Comparisons with monolithic VMS indicate that omitting the pressure fine scale reduces drag overprediction and excess modeled dissipation, at the cost of increased divergence error. In the Taylor-Green tests, the projection formulation also reduces the average solution time per step by factors ranging from approximately [MATH] to [MATH] under identical solver settings.
tldr: This paper presents a numerical method for solving the Navier-Stokes equations using a Helmholtz-Leray projection with variational multiscale stabilization.
motivation: The paper addresses computational challenges in fluid dynamics, specifically the stability and efficiency of finite element methods for incompressible flows.
method: It introduces a residual-based variational multiscale stabilization of an incremental Helmholtz-Leray projection method, decomposing the velocity into coarse and fine scales and solving a predictor, pressure Poisson, and projection step.
result: Numerical tests show good agreement with reference data and reduced computational time compared to monolithic VMS, though with increased divergence error.
conclusion: The proposed method offers an efficient alternative for solving Navier-Stokes equations, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Irregularly Observed Long-memory Levy-driven Moving Average Processes
authors: Anne Philippe Mohamedou Ould Haye
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study long-memory continuous-time moving-average processes driven by a Levy process and observed at random renewal times. The sampling scheme introduces an additional source of randomness through irregular observation times. We establish the asymptotic behaviour of normalized partial sums under both finite- and infinite-mean renewal sampling.
tldr: This paper studies the asymptotic behavior of partial sums of long-memory continuous-time moving-average processes driven by Lévy processes and observed at random renewal times.
motivation: The paper addresses a gap in the literature on long-memory processes with irregular observation times, which is relevant for statistical inference in time series.
method: The authors derive asymptotic results for normalized partial sums under both finite- and infinite-mean renewal sampling schemes, using probabilistic techniques for Lévy-driven moving averages.
result: They establish the asymptotic distribution of the partial sums, which depends on the sampling scheme and the properties of the Lévy process.
conclusion: The findings extend the theory of long-memory processes to irregularly sampled data, but the topic is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Enforcing Access Control In Distributed Version Control Systems
authors: Xin Xu, Quanwei Cai, Jingqiang Lin, Shiran Pan, Liangqin Ren
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Version control systems (VCS), including central VCS (CVCS) and distributed VCS (DVCS), are widely adopted to manage the changes to various types of data. Unlike the CVCS where all the entities obtain the data from the server and the access control is enforced with the cooperation of the server, each entity in the DVCS stores the entire repository, obtains the repository shared by any entity and is free to share its own repository. Therefore, existing access control schemes for CVCS are not suitable for DVCS. In this paper, we present a distributed access control scheme (Disac) for DVCS. Disac makes each entity have full control over its data, while the access control is enforced at each entity independently. We adopt Attribute-based Encryption (ABE) and Attribute-based Signature (ABS) to achieve the read and write permission control. The analysis of the Git client demonstrates that Disac can be integrated easily.
tldr: This paper proposes a distributed access control scheme for version control systems using attribute-based encryption and signatures.
motivation: Distributed version control systems lack centralized access control, so each entity needs to enforce its own permissions.
method: The scheme uses Attribute-based Encryption (ABE) for read control and Attribute-based Signature (ABS) for write control, integrated into Git.
result: The analysis shows the scheme can be easily integrated into Git clients.
conclusion: The paper provides a practical solution for access control in DVCS, but it is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Stateful Cooperative Agents Safeguarding LLMs Against Evolving Multi-Turn Attacks
authors: Siyuan Li, Zehao Liu, Haoyu Li, Xi Lin, Ning Liu, Jun Wu, Jianhua Li, Mohsen Guizani
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00134v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As LLMs become increasingly integrated into complex applications, their vulnerability to adversarial attacks has raised significant concerns. However, existing defenses remain reactive in nature. This limitation makes it difficult for them to counter sophisticated threats, as adversaries continuously adjust their strategies across multi-turn interactions. In this paper, we present a proactive defense framework for securing LLMs against evolving multi-turn adversarial attacks that combines disruption, misdirection, and adaptation across successive interaction turns. In particular, it employs a cooperative multi-agent architecture in which specialized agents execute complementary defense strategies. These strategies include controlled response pacing to increase attack costs, strategically ambiguous outputs to mislead adversaries into ineffective strategies, and forensic analysis of interaction logs to identify attack patterns and refine defenses. These agents are coordinated by an adaptive mechanism that dynamically adjusts the defense strategy in response to escalating threats. To facilitate comprehensive evaluation, we present the EMRA dataset designed to simulate evolving strategies across multi-turn attacks, including 5,200 adversarial samples across eight attack types. Experimental results on EMRA across multiple LLM backbones show that the proposed framework reduces ASR by 69% on average relative to evaluated state-of-the-art baselines. Beyond suppressing harmful outputs, it sustains deceptive engagement, achieving an average DR more than six times that of the strongest baselines and increasing attacker-token consumption by 198.83% on average relative to evaluated baselines. Code and dataset are available at [URL].
tldr: This paper proposes a proactive defense framework for LLMs against multi-turn adversarial attacks using cooperative agents.
motivation: Existing defenses are reactive and fail against evolving multi-turn attacks, so a proactive approach is needed.
method: A multi-agent architecture with specialized agents for disruption, misdirection, and forensic analysis, coordinated by an adaptive mechanism.
result: The framework reduces attack success rate by 69% and increases attacker-token consumption by 198.83% on the EMRA dataset.
conclusion: The proposed framework effectively safeguards LLMs against evolving multi-turn attacks, outperforming baselines.

title: Symbolic Attack Chain Generation From Atomic Red Team Techniques: An Empirical Study Of Predicate Representation Granularity
authors: Ramya Varunsegar
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00143v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated attack chain generation is critical for modern cybersecurity, yet manual construction fails to scale as adversary behaviors expand. While classical AI planning using PDDL offers a formal method to automate this process, it relies on the accurate translation of techniques into symbolic predicates. Current state-of-the-art systems like AURORA employ a nine-category Attack Action Linking Model (AALM), but the necessity of this specific granularity remains unvalidated. This work investigates the impact of predicate representation granularity on plan validity, cost, and fidelity. Utilizing a pipeline where a Large Language Model (LLM) performs translation and the Fast Downward engine performs deterministic reasoning, the study compares the full nine-category AALM against a reduced five-category scheme derived empirically from Atomic Red Team (ART) execution evidence. Results from a sixteen-technique corpus demonstrate that plan validity and cost are largely insensitive to granularity, with 81.3% identical outcomes across both schemes. The findings suggest that higher granularity primarily enhances the internal structural resolution of a plan's justification rather than the viability of the generated attack chain itself.
tldr: This paper studies the impact of predicate representation granularity on automated attack chain generation using LLM and classical planning, but it is unrelated to quantum information science.
motivation: The paper addresses scalability issues in cybersecurity attack chain generation, which is outside the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, and hybrid systems.
method: The authors use an LLM to translate Atomic Red Team techniques into PDDL predicates with two granularity schemes (nine-category vs five-category) and compare plan validity and cost using the Fast Downward planner.
result: The study finds that plan validity and cost are largely insensitive to granularity, with 81.3% identical outcomes across both schemes.
conclusion: Higher granularity mainly improves internal structural resolution of plan justification rather than the viability of the attack chain, but this has no relevance to quantum information research.

title: Exposed By Design: A Dynamic Security Assessment Of Internet-Facing Mcp Servers At Scale
authors: Nicol\'as Padilla
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00150v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) has seen rapid adoption since its November 2024 launch, with over 21,000 server instances detectable on the public internet. We present the first dynamic behavioral security assessment of internet-facing MCP servers, combining passive discovery across eleven data sources (crt.sh, HuggingFace, GitHub, npm, Smithery, PyPI, Censys, FOFA, Shodan, glama.ai, and pulsemcp.com) with active dynamic testing using Corvus, a purpose-built framework implementing 34 test modules covering 10 MCP-specific vulnerability classes. Across four measurement runs spanning July 2026, we confirm 640 production MCP servers and dynamically audit 414, uncovering 68 reportable vulnerabilities including SQL injection, SSRF targeting cloud metadata services, prompt template injection, and path traversal via cursor manipulation. We find that 91.8% of dynamically audited servers lack OAuth authentication, 687 tool instances across confirmed servers expose shell execution capabilities without access controls, and 41.6% of confirmed servers disappear within three days between consecutive measurement runs---indicating rapid deployment cycles without security review. We report on our responsible disclosure pipeline and release Corvus as an open-source framework for MCP security evaluation.
tldr: This paper presents a security assessment of internet-facing MCP servers, focusing on vulnerabilities and lack of authentication, which is unrelated to quantum information science.
motivation: The rapid adoption of MCP servers on the internet raises security concerns, and the authors aim to provide the first dynamic behavioral security assessment to identify vulnerabilities.
method: The authors combine passive discovery across multiple data sources with active dynamic testing using a custom framework (Corvus) that implements 34 test modules covering 10 vulnerability classes.
result: They confirm 640 production MCP servers, audit 414, and uncover 68 vulnerabilities, including SQL injection and SSRF, with 91.8% lacking OAuth and 41.6% disappearing within three days.
conclusion: The findings highlight significant security weaknesses in MCP servers and the need for better security practices, with the release of an open-source framework for further evaluation.

title: From Monoliths To Swarms: A Study Of Attack Surface Evolution In The Transition To Multi-Agent Web Systems
authors: Sandra Siby Yashaswi Malla
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00202v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM)-based web agents are increasingly evolving from single-agent systems (SAS) to multi-agent systems (MAS). While MAS can lead to improved task performance by decomposing complex tasks across specialized sub-agents, such role decomposition introduces new structural attack surfaces that are absent in SAS. This expanded attack surface remains poorly understood and inadequately categorized. To address this, we propose a taxonomy to categorize attack vectors specific to web-based MAS, accounting for vulnerabilities introduced or amplified by the involvement of multiple agents. We further present a test-bed WebMASLab to analyze web agent security against a fully external, web-only adversary. To isolate the effect of architecture, we keep the user task, tool surface, and browser substrate fixed, and compare single- and multi-agent setups. We evaluate three adversarial scenarios, across three conditions (baseline, prompt-hardened, and reasoning-enabled), including a novel MAS-specific Telephone Loop attack that exploits cross-agent delegation to create cyclical task loops. The attack is inert against SAS but compromises MAS when powered by three of the four frontier models evaluated (Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-5.2, GPT-5.4), averaging 80% across them at baseline. Only the fourth model, Claude Sonnet 4.6, resists the attack with a 92% detection rate. For the rest, the detection is 0% at baseline, reaching 33% with prompt-hardening for one model. We also show that obvious defenses do not generalize; prompt-hardening collapses one model's ASR from 100% to 8% while providing only modest reduction to the others. Our findings demonstrate that the transition from single- to multi-agent web systems changes the security landscape. Role specialization may not only lead to performance optimization but also introduce new architectural risks that require further study and defenses.
tldr: This paper studies security vulnerabilities in multi-agent web systems, proposing a taxonomy and a testbed to analyze attack surfaces introduced by role decomposition.
motivation: The transition from single-agent to multi-agent web systems introduces new structural attack surfaces that are poorly understood and inadequately categorized.
method: The authors propose a taxonomy of attack vectors for web-based MAS, present a testbed (WebMASLab) to analyze security against an external web-only adversary, and compare single- and multi-agent setups under fixed task, tool, and browser conditions.
result: They evaluate three adversarial scenarios, including a novel Telephone Loop attack that exploits cross-agent delegation, which compromises MAS with three of four frontier models (averaging 80% success) while being inert against SAS; only one model resists with 92% detection.
conclusion: The transition to multi-agent web systems changes the security landscape, and role specialization introduces new architectural risks that require further study and defenses.

title: Reflection, Education, Consistency: Towards Best Ethics Practices At Security And Privacy Conferences
authors: Florian Hantke, Rafael Mrowczynski, Til Dralle, Ben Stock
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00282v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Research ethics is a controversial and emotionally charged topic in the security and privacy community, sparking discussions at conferences and on social media. In recent years, some of the leading conferences have introduced interventions such as mandatory ethics sections, with mixed reactions within the community. Program committee chairs and steering committees increasingly emphasize ethics, yet there is limited empirical validation on ethics procedures and interventions, as well as no explicitly communicated goals. To support a shared understanding in our community and guide informed decisions at the conference level, we examined past ethics policies at the top-four conferences and conducted in-depth semi-structured interviews with senior and junior (n=20) community members, including some (former) chairs of program and research ethics committees. In these, we explored reasons for and goals of ethics procedures and discussed existing ethics interventions as well as possible new approaches proposed by our team. While the community appears to be evolving toward the identified goals, i.e., raising ethical awareness and preventing the publication of unethical work, we identified the lack of ethical education within the community itself as a major obstacle to further progress on this matter. Ethical education is often passed to the universities. Interviewees also mentioned challenges with the complexity of ethics policies and the lack of consistency across different conferences, as well as policies changing year-to-year. Several participants warned that over-regulation may lead to backlash, encouraging mere compliance, such as people turning to LLMs for ethics sections rather than undertaking in-depth consideration. In response, we suggest a coordinated, community-wide ethics steering effort and take a first step by introducing an open ethics wiki.
tldr: This paper studies ethics practices at security and privacy conferences, proposing community-wide interventions, which is unrelated to quantum information science.
motivation: The security and privacy community lacks empirical validation and shared goals for ethics procedures, leading to inconsistent policies and backlash.
method: The authors reviewed ethics policies at top-four conferences and conducted semi-structured interviews with 20 community members, including chairs, to explore goals and interventions.
result: They identified a lack of ethical education and consistency across conferences, and propose a coordinated ethics steering effort and an open ethics wiki.
conclusion: The community should adopt coordinated ethics practices to improve awareness and prevent unethical publications, while avoiding over-regulation.

title: On The Complexity Of Computing Outputs Of A Metric Turing Machine
authors: Yaroslav Ivanashev
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classes MidP, MedP, and [MATH] contain functions that compute the median solution for certain types of problems. In this paper, for these classes we introduce analogous classes of functions that compute the k-th solution, where k is an order function that depends on the input. We prove that the classes MidP, MedP, and [MATH] are polynomial-time 1-Turing inter-reducible with the corresponding classes, where the order function is from FP or FP[MATH]. For MedP we also prove that it coincides with the corresponding classes, where the order function is from FP or #P. For several inclusions between function classes we give equivalent inclusions between language classes. In particular, we establish inclusion relations between MaxP and median classes MidP, MedP, and [MATH]. We also prove that NPSV[MATH] MaxP [MATH] FP[MATH] and both inclusions are proper if and only if NP [MATH] coNP.
tldr: This paper studies complexity classes for computing k-th solutions of problems, which is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to generalize median solution classes to k-th solution classes and explore their relationships.
method: It defines new function classes based on order functions and proves inter-reducibility and inclusion results.
result: It shows polynomial-time 1-Turing inter-reducibility for certain classes and establishes inclusions between MaxP and median classes.
conclusion: The paper contributes to computational complexity theory, not to the user's research interests.

title: Pure-Strategy Equilibrium In The Generalized First-Price Auction
authors: Andrzej Skrzypacz Michael Ostrovsky
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00334v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the classic result on the (non-)existence of pure-strategy Nash equilibria in the Generalized First-Price Auction for sponsored search advertising and show that the conclusion may be reversed when ads are ranked based on the product of stochastic quality scores and bid amounts, rather than solely on the bids or on the product of bids and deterministic quality scores. Moreover, the expected revenue in the pure strategy equilibrium of the Generalized First-Price Auction may substantially exceed that of the Generalized Second-Price Auction, although under some conditions the relation may also be reversed.
tldr: This paper analyzes pure-strategy equilibria in the Generalized First-Price Auction for sponsored search advertising, showing that stochastic quality scores can reverse the non-existence result and affect revenue comparisons.
motivation: The paper revisits a classic result in auction theory to understand how stochastic quality scores impact equilibrium existence and revenue in sponsored search advertising.
method: The authors model the auction with stochastic quality scores and analyze the existence and properties of pure-strategy Nash equilibria, comparing expected revenues with the Generalized Second-Price Auction.
result: They find that with stochastic quality scores, pure-strategy equilibria can exist, and the expected revenue may be higher or lower than in the Generalized Second-Price Auction depending on conditions.
conclusion: The findings have implications for auction design in sponsored search, suggesting that stochastic quality scores can alter equilibrium outcomes and revenue performance.

title: Verifiable Checks For Business Rule Consistency
authors: Joseph Tafese, Milad Hooshyar, Sam Bayless, Nick Feng, Arie Gurfinkel
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00396v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Maintaining consistency between natural language documentation of business rules and their evolving internal implementations is a significant challenge in large-scale systems. We present SIRNA, a tool and framework for checking such consistency using SMT solvers. Using the case study of cost calculations in tax domains, we demonstrate a three-part system that combines large language models (LLMs) with formal verification methods. SIRNA translates natural language documentation into candidate SMT formulas using LLMs, followed by checks to validate the translations. Then, corresponding business rules are converted into equivalent SMT representations and validated against the natural language formalizations. Our method is generalizable to domains where business logic exists in both natural language documentation and programmatic implementation. Compared to baseline evaluations, SIRNA significantly reduces the number of false positives and false negatives while offering explainability for its findings.
tldr: This paper presents SIRNA, a tool that uses LLMs and SMT solvers to verify consistency between natural language business rules and their implementations.
motivation: Maintaining consistency between natural language documentation and evolving code is challenging in large-scale systems.
method: SIRNA translates natural language documentation into candidate SMT formulas using LLMs, validates these translations, and then converts corresponding business rules into SMT representations for comparison.
result: The tool reduces false positives and negatives compared to baselines and provides explainability.
conclusion: The approach is generalizable to domains with both natural language and programmatic business logic.

title: Support Contraction For Well-Supported Nash Equilibria
authors: Zhengyang Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00453v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the support contraction, a structural procedure for computing well-supported Nash equilibria (WSNE) in bimatrix games. On a common action rectangle, the procedure alternately retains the support of a row maximin strategy for the row-payoff matrix and the support of a column maximin strategy for the column-payoff matrix. Each restriction preserves the value of the matrix game that selected it and can only increase the other value. At a stable rectangle, full support of the two maximizing strategies and complementary slackness make every surviving action tight. Crossing the two minimax strategies then gives an exact Nash equilibrium of the retained subgame, while the two zero-sum values bound deviations to deleted actions. Support contraction gives a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that computes a [MATH]-WSNE of every rational bimatrix game with payoffs in [MATH], with no additive slack, and a deterministic [MATH]-bit two-party protocol for a [MATH]-WSNE. The same support-contraction certificate, preceded by randomized one-sided localization, gives an [MATH] payoff-query algorithm for the same guarantee, improving the [MATH] dependence to [MATH].
tldr: This paper introduces a polynomial-time algorithm for computing well-supported Nash equilibria in bimatrix games using a support contraction procedure.
motivation: The paper addresses the computational complexity of finding approximate Nash equilibria in bimatrix games, a fundamental problem in algorithmic game theory.
method: The method iteratively restricts the support of row and column maximin strategies on a common action rectangle, preserving game values and leading to a stable rectangle where an exact Nash equilibrium of the subgame is found.
result: The algorithm computes a well-supported Nash equilibrium with no additive slack in polynomial time, and also provides a communication protocol and improved query complexity.
conclusion: The paper contributes to algorithmic game theory, but it is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Auditable Release Control For Pedagogical Leakage In Llm Tutors
authors: Nizam Kadir
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model tutors can be correct and helpful yet disclose an answer or decisive reasoning before that disclosure is authorized. We formalize this state- and action-dependent failure as pedagogical leakage and introduce an authorization-aware complete-mediation boundary. A selector emits one of five disclosure contracts, trusted policy gates privileged modes, and a renderer proposes language. A single release function applies inspectable checks, optional cumulative verification, and action-specific fallback; replayable traces separate selection, generation, verification, and enforcement failures. Matched component attribution exposes a safety-utility frontier. On 599 fixed Gemini 3.5 proposals, strict mediation reduces blinded three-model panel-majority leakage flags from 181 to 0 (paired problem-cluster difference -30.22 points, 95% CI [-35.00,-25.72]), while replacing 581 responses and lowering helpfulness. Checker-triggered fallback alone yields 11 majority flags; adding the semantic verifier yields 14 and no reliable marginal gain. A global A1 scaffold yields 0 majority and 54 any-judge flags, outperforming fitted Q on automatic safety and utility. In an externally timestamped replication over 40 unseen problem clusters and 480 attack sequences, high-assurance release reduces majority flags from 42 to 8 (-7.08 points, 95% CI [-13.13,-2.29]); seven failures persist, one is introduced, and mean helpfulness falls by .192. These results establish an auditable release boundary and failure attribution under declared contracts, not universal semantic safety or learning gains.
tldr: This paper introduces a framework for controlling pedagogical leakage in LLM tutors, focusing on auditable release control and safety-utility trade-offs.
motivation: LLM tutors may disclose answers prematurely, and existing methods lack formal mechanisms for authorization-aware control.
method: The authors propose a complete-mediation boundary with a selector, trusted policy gates, and a renderer, implementing a release function with inspectable checks and fallback mechanisms.
result: Strict mediation reduces leakage flags from 181 to 0 in a fixed dataset, with a trade-off in helpfulness; replication shows reduced flags but persistent failures.
conclusion: The framework provides auditable release control and failure attribution, but does not achieve universal semantic safety or learning gains.

title: A False Average: Chain-of-Thought Monitors Collapse Where They Are The Only Defense
authors: Leo Richter Shikhar Shiromani
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00583v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is meant to catch the reward hacks that look clean in the actions and betray themselves only in the reasoning. We show that this is exactly where an adversary who controls the reasoning can defeat it. Rewriting only an agent's reasoning to read as good-faith engineering, while copying every command and output verbatim so the exploit is unchanged, drops a held-out monitor's catch rate on that subset from about 95% to under 11% in one gradient-free shot. A monitor's aggregate accuracy is a false average: dominated by hacks the actions give away, it hides the near-total collapse this rewrite produces on the subset where CoT monitoring is the only signal. The attack transfers across monitor families and agent models, reproduces with live agents, though against a calibrated monitor evasion concentrates in the strongest agent. Trace-only defenses recover it only partially, even one primed on the attack, because the rewrite stays truthful about what happened and lies only about intent; only information from outside the trace helps substantially. A probe on an open-weight surrogate monitor's activations separates the hacks its verdict misses, but a causal control shows this is a detector, not evidence the monitor secretly knows.
tldr: This paper studies adversarial attacks on chain-of-thought monitoring in AI agents, showing that rewriting reasoning can evade detection.
motivation: The paper addresses a security issue in AI safety, specifically the reliability of chain-of-thought monitoring to detect reward hacking.
method: The authors demonstrate a gradient-free attack that rewrites an agent's reasoning to appear benign while preserving the exploit, and test it across monitors and models.
result: The attack reduces the monitor's catch rate from 95% to under 11% on the subset where monitoring is the only signal, and transfers across models.
conclusion: Chain-of-thought monitoring is vulnerable to adversarial reasoning rewriting, and trace-only defenses are insufficient; external information is needed.

title: Compact Sat And MaxSAT Encodings For Business-to-Business Meeting Scheduling With Idle-Time Balancing
authors: Long Duc Nguyen, Tuyen van Kieu, Khanh van To
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00614v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Business-to-business meeting scheduling assigns requested pairwise meetings to time slots and locations under availability, capacity, conflict, and precedence constraints. The published Boolean formulation retains meeting-slot assignments that propagation can eliminate and encodes precedence relations with pairwise clauses. We present compact SAT and MaxSAT encodings based on solution-preserving domain filtering, variables shared at selected precedence boundaries, and an objective that minimizes the range of participants' internal idle-slot totals. Experiments on 126 official and 100 higher-density derived instances examine domain filtering, precedence representation, transitive relations, and optimization method. Compared with an adapted published MaxSAT formulation using the same objective, the proposed encoding reduces the median clause count by 40.3% and median peak memory usage by 55.9%. Domain filtering alone reduces assignment variables by 24.1% and clauses by 16.2%. Sharing variables at selected precedence boundaries reduces clauses by 0.5%-1.0% on official precedence instances and by up to 5.5% at the highest derived density. The idle-time measure distinguishes one-slot interruptions from longer waits, while aggregate idle time provides a complementary measure. Compared with Gurobi, a leading commercial solver, all three SAT and MaxSAT methods solve every official instance with lower median total times.
tldr: This paper presents compact SAT and MaxSAT encodings for business-to-business meeting scheduling, focusing on idle-time balancing.
motivation: The authors aim to improve the efficiency of solving meeting scheduling problems by reducing the size of Boolean formulations and optimizing idle-time distribution.
method: They propose solution-preserving domain filtering, variable sharing at precedence boundaries, and an objective minimizing the range of internal idle-slot totals, and compare against an adapted published MaxSAT formulation and Gurobi.
result: The proposed encoding reduces median clause count by 40.3% and peak memory usage by 55.9%, and solves all official instances faster than Gurobi.
conclusion: The compact encodings significantly improve solver performance for meeting scheduling, but the topic is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Taming The Search Space: Solving And Generating Hitori And Binairo Puzzles
authors: Lukas Zandomeneghi, Rainhard Dieter Findling, Marc Kurz
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates solving and generation techniques for the logic puzzles Hitori and Binairo. Two solving paradigms are compared: backtracking with domain-specific optimizations, and SAT-based solving via conjunctive normal form encodings. An empirical evaluation analyzes runtime, explored search nodes, and branching factor across varying puzzle sizes. To support systematic benchmarking in the evaluation, generators capable of producing valid and uniquely solvable puzzle instances are developed. Results indicate that constraint propagation is the most effective backtracking optimization, substantially reducing the effective branching factor, search tree size, and thus runtime. Heuristic variable ordering and scoring strategies provide additional improvements. For Binairo, the SAT-based approach solves all evaluated instances within low runtime, while optimized backtracking fails to solve difficult puzzle instances within the timeout. For Hitori, propagation-based backtracking achieves the best results, while for the SAT-based approach the iterative connectivity check takes up the majority of the runtime, failing difficult puzzle instances.
tldr: This paper studies solving and generating Hitori and Binairo logic puzzles using backtracking and SAT-based methods.
motivation: The authors aim to systematically compare solving paradigms for these puzzles and develop generators for benchmarking.
method: They implement backtracking with domain-specific optimizations and SAT encodings, and evaluate runtime, search nodes, and branching factor.
result: Constraint propagation is most effective for backtracking; SAT solves Binairo well but struggles with Hitori due to connectivity checks.
conclusion: The paper provides insights into puzzle-solving algorithms but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Order Auctions With Private Position Preferences
authors: Aviv Yaish Ruijie Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00786v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study auctions where two positions are sold to unit-demand bidders with private heterogeneous order preferences: some are specialists who value only the first position, while others are generalists who are indifferent between the two. First, we consider a standard first-price rule which allocates the first and second items to the highest and second-highest bidders, respectively. We show that no strategy profile ex-post implements the efficient allocation at every type profile, irrespective of payments, and provide a distribution-free equilibrium welfare guarantee of [MATH]. To augment this result, we prove that for deterministic one-round auctions and discrete bids, the efficient allocation requires each bidder to communicate at least one bit more than its bid's binary representation. We next ask what the same bit accomplishes in winner-pays-bid formats where bidders can also specify specific item preferences. In particular, we show that this strengthens our distribution-free equilibrium welfare guarantee to [MATH]. Finally, we discuss our results' applicability to priority service auctions and blockchain transaction sequencing.
tldr: This paper studies auction mechanisms for two positions with bidders having private order preferences, focusing on efficiency and communication complexity.
motivation: The authors aim to understand the limitations and communication requirements of implementing efficient allocations in auctions with heterogeneous position preferences, with applications to priority service and blockchain transaction sequencing.
method: They analyze first-price and winner-pays-bid auction formats, prove impossibility results for ex-post efficiency, derive distribution-free welfare guarantees, and establish lower bounds on communication via information-theoretic arguments.
result: They show that no strategy profile ex-post implements the efficient allocation, provide welfare guarantees, and prove that efficient allocation requires at least one extra bit of communication beyond the bid's binary representation.
conclusion: The findings highlight inherent trade-offs between efficiency and communication in such auctions, with practical implications for priority service and blockchain sequencing.

title: Multi-LLM Consensus Framework For Evaluating Banking-Sector Nids Dataset Coverage Of Mitre Att&ck Techniques
authors: Sanjida Khanom, Sadia Afrin Khan, Adrita Rahman Tory, Md. Ahsan Habib, Khondokar Fida Hasan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00895v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The systemic criticality of global banking networks has ren-dered them high-priority targets for advanced persistent threats, neces-sitating Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS) whose operational effectiveness must extend beyond statistical accuracy. However, a signif-icant validation gap persists between experimental NIDS performance and real-world effectiveness: NIDS models that achieve high accuracy on standard benchmarks often fail in operational banking environments because generic datasets lack sector-specific patterns, such as SWIFT and ATM-related intrusions, that characterize real financial threats. To address this, the paper investigates a sector-aware evaluation method-ology that systematically assesses how well existing NIDS benchmark datasets cover the attack behaviors most relevant to banking infrastruc-ture. The methodology maps documented adversary behaviors from the MITRE ATT&CK knowledge base to NIDS benchmarks while enforcing the realistic sensor limitations defined by NIST SP 800-94. Leveraging a multi-LLM consensus engine with four state-of-the-art models, we evalu-ated 210 banking-specific adversary techniques to derive a baseline of 68 network-observable behaviors for systematic coverage analysis. Results across five benchmark datasets demonstrate that UNSW-NB15 achieves the highest utility with an 82.2% weighted coverage score (though only 18.4% reflects direct, technique-level evidence), while CIC-DDoS2019 re-veals an 89.9% blind spot for core banking behaviors. These findings es-tablish a reproducible foundation for sector-aware NIDS evaluation and highlight the urgent need for banking-native datasets.
tldr: This paper proposes a multi-LLM consensus framework to evaluate NIDS benchmark datasets for coverage of banking-specific MITRE ATT&CK techniques, finding that current datasets have significant gaps.
motivation: NIDS models often fail in real banking environments due to lack of sector-specific attack patterns in training data. The authors aim to systematically assess dataset coverage of banking-relevant adversary behaviors.
method: They map MITRE ATT&CK techniques to NIDS benchmarks, enforce NIST SP 800-94 sensor limitations, and use four LLMs in a consensus engine to evaluate 210 banking-specific techniques across five datasets.
result: UNSW-NB15 achieves the highest weighted coverage (82.2%) but only 18.4% direct evidence; CIC-DDoS2019 has an 89.9% blind spot for core banking behaviors.
conclusion: The findings highlight the need for banking-native NIDS datasets and provide a reproducible framework for sector-aware evaluation.

title: A Decade Of Healthcare Cyber Threats: Empirical Analysis, Evidence-Based Prioritisation, And Ai Threat Model
authors: Sadia Mehrin Rahi, Ayesha Siddika, Istiyak Hasan Maruf, Adrita Rahman Tory, Muhammad Aminur Rahaman, Khondokar Fida Hasan
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00901v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Healthcare systems face persistent and evolving cyber threats, yet how adversarial tactics and techniques have shifted over time has not been systematically characterised using empirical, multi-source data. This paper analyses 1,214 threat records drawn from three authoritative sources: the MITRE ATT&CK behavioural framework, the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue, and the NIST vulnerability database, covering 44 validated healthcare-targeting threat entities from 2017 to 2024. We show that attacker behaviour has shifted measurably toward stealth-oriented tactics: defense evasion remained the dominant tactic throughout the observation period, consistently accounting for 15-20% of observed technique use from 2017 to 2024, while persistence declined from 11.2% to zero and initial access from 9.0% to zero over the same period. We further demonstrate that existing detection guidance is structurally misaligned with where attacker effort is concentrated, with the least-covered techniques receiving the most adversarial attention. A convergence analysis links 679 confirmed exploited vulnerabilities to a single dominant behavioural technique, identifying a common addressable chokepoint across the vulnerability and behavioural surfaces. Finally, we identify 42 high-priority techniques representing immediate detection opportunities and show that this set of techniques maps directly to emerging threats against AI-integrated clinical systems.
tldr: This paper analyzes healthcare cyber threats using empirical data from MITRE ATT&CK, CISA, and NIST, focusing on threat actor behavior and detection gaps.
motivation: Healthcare systems face evolving cyber threats, but there is a lack of systematic, empirical characterization of how adversarial tactics have shifted over time.
method: The authors analyze 1,214 threat records from three authoritative sources, covering 44 healthcare-targeting threat entities from 2017 to 2024, and perform convergence analysis to link vulnerabilities to behavioral techniques.
result: The study finds a shift toward stealth-oriented tactics, with defense evasion dominant, and identifies misalignment between detection guidance and attacker effort, plus a common chokepoint and 42 high-priority techniques.
conclusion: The findings highlight the need for better detection strategies and provide a threat model for AI-integrated clinical systems.

title: What Syntax Cannot See: The Dynamic Syntactic Invariance Principle And Several Instances Of The Same Hidden Assumption, And A Contradiction
authors: Fabio F. G. Buono
abstract: ArXiv:2608.00958v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a single method, find what an accepted result silently assumed, make it a variable, and prove what follows once it is dropped, and shows it keeps working across domains with nothing in common. Its formal core is the Dynamic Syntactic Invariance Principle: a known static inaccessibility result survives when a system's rules evolve in time, under one sharp necessary condition. A direct cryptographic payoff follows: the secrecy of a rolling-key scheme persists across sessions under a structural update, strengthening a static guarantee from earlier work. The same move is then carried into settings far from each other, special relativity, the reach of a formal theory of physical law, and computable output that is fully meaningful yet indistinguishable from noise to every observer, each established on its own terms, so the recurring structure beneath them is found, not imposed: a distinction real at a full level of description can be invisible at a restricted one. Applied to , this yields a contradiction from which coherence forces [MATH], derived from what standard theory already admits rather than assumed,offered with one reservation, about the proof, not the answer.
tldr: This paper proposes a Dynamic Syntactic Invariance Principle and applies it across cryptography, relativity, and computability, but it is not related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: The author aims to uncover hidden assumptions in accepted results by making them variables and exploring consequences when dropped, demonstrating a cross-domain method.
method: The method involves identifying silent assumptions, parameterizing them, and proving results under dynamic rule changes, formalized as the Dynamic Syntactic Invariance Principle.
result: The paper claims to strengthen a rolling-key scheme's security, derive a contradiction in a formal theory of physical law, and show that meaningful computable output can be indistinguishable from noise.
conclusion: The recurring structure of invisible distinctions at restricted levels is found across domains, but the paper's focus is on general syntactic principles, not quantum information or thermodynamics.
